Bespreking van het huiswerk (17 maart 2019)
Bespreking van studente 1
Het tweede punt heeft de zuster geoefend (dat men eerlijk is in de opvoeding). Daarin hadden wij een gedeelte over het tonen van je zwakke punten als opvoeder. Vorige week had zij de vraag gesteld: kun je als iemand die lesgeeft tegen je leerlingen zeggen, om hen te motiveren: «bij mij was [het] ook zo». Dat zou je niet moeten doen. Zij heeft [de zaak] deze week op een andere manier aangepakt. Twee leerlingen gaven aan dat zij het enigszins moeilijk vinden om al het huiswerk dat hun is opgegeven te onthouden, en dat zij er soms geen tijd voor hebben. Zij motiveerde hen deze keer met een hadieth waarin de Profeet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam zegt dat wie de Qur'aan leert, in graden wordt verheven (zij kent de hadieth nu niet letterlijk), maar zij toonde niet haar zwakke punten. Voorheen deed zij dat, maar toonde zij ook haar zwakke punten, terwijl zij dat nu niet doet.
Daarnaast heeft zij het bedekken van de fouten van de ander geoefend. Zij had daar ook een vraag over, dat er een algemeen advies gegeven kan worden. Dat heeft zij ook gedaan, omdat zij op het punt stond die persoon te confronteren. Zij gaf een algemeen vermaan. En zij kon deelnemen aan het gesprek, omdat hij niet wist dat ik op de hoogte was van een bepaalde zonde. Als iemand zich erg schaamt, dan vindt zij het moeilijk om het advies voort te zetten. Deze methode helpt dus veel.
De leraar: Deze methode helpt bij een aantal mensen en zou ook meer gebruikt moeten worden. Wanneer je ziet dat deze methode niet helpt, dan is het belangrijk om het vermaan op een andere manier toe te passen. Bijvoorbeeld dat je iemand tegenkomt die zijn zonde kent en je hem vraagt om haar te helpen, om haar te vermanen. En het kan ook zijn dat je ziet dat een ander zo'n zonde heeft gezien en dat hij invloed heeft op die [persoon]. Dan ga je naar die [persoon] toe. Als dat alles niet helpt en die [persoon] die zonde blijft begaan, dan is het desondanks belangrijk dat je die persoon confronteert.
De zuster: Begrijp ik het juist dat wanneer anderen door de zonde beïnvloed worden [we confronteren]?
De leraar: Wanneer de zonde niet bedekt is, omdat zij het openlijk doet maar jij het niet hebt gezien, dan is het desondanks belangrijk dat je die [persoon] confronteert. Als die [persoon] zichzelf stopt, dan is confrontatie niet nodig.
Het derde punt, het plezier door middel van een activiteit, wilde zij oefenen met haar nichtje [haar jonge verwante].
De leraar: Je hoeft het niet per se als een activiteit te zien, je kunt het ook zien als een grapje [tussendoor], of tijdens het vermaan of tijdens de opvoeding. En het kan ook eenvoudig zijn. De activiteit is ook een manier, maar het kan ook op een eenvoudige manier, en als zij als grapje ook in de juiste richting heeft geleid, dan is dat helemaal mooi.
De leraar: Wat betreft de fouten, heb je dat ook geëvalueerd? Je zei dat je een fout hebt gestopt, maar zijn er ook andere zaken geëvalueerd? Het [ging] over jezelf, fouten die je voorheen maakte wat betreft de opvoeding.
De zuster: Die heb ik bijgestuurd, bijvoorbeeld dat ik zwakke punten aan het licht bracht en iemand met een fout wilde confronteren. Zo heb ik mezelf geconfronteerd.
Bespreking van studente 2
Ik worstelde aanvankelijk een beetje met de opdracht, omdat de punten die we behandeld hebben gericht zijn op de opvoeder. Ik ben nog geen opvoedster, dus vond ik het moeilijk om de punten in de praktijk te brengen.
Aan de andere kant ontdekte ik door middel van de opdracht dat er in mijn gedrag nog steeds fouten [aanwezig] zijn die we behandeld hebben, en dat gedrag heb ik zoveel mogelijk verbeterd en daarna het tegenovergestelde ervan gedaan.
Wat betreft het tweede punt:
Dat men oprecht is in de opvoeding (dat men een oprechte opvoeding heeft: dat wil zeggen dat men opvoedt omwille van Allaah).
Zo behoort de opvoeder zich ook niet bezig te houden met zinloze zaken. Ik merk dat ik me van tijd tot tijd nog steeds bezighoud met zinloze zaken (filmpjes op YouTube over onderwerpen die ik leuk vind), zoeken naar inspiratie voor decoratie, enz. Daarom was ik de afgelopen week meer bewust. Op de momenten waarop ik YouTube of Pinterest wilde aanzetten, of het internet wilde openen op zoek naar inspiratie, herinnerde ik mij dat ik me met zinloze zaken bezighield. In plaats daarvan ging ik betekenisvolle dingen doen (luisteren naar de Qur'aan).
De punten 4, 5 en 6 overlappen bij mij:
Het vermijden van veelvuldig verwijten
Het vermijden van kwaadwillige vermoedens en het naspeuren van de gebreken van de betreffende persoon, dat wil zeggen het graven naar de fouten van de persoon
Verwacht de fout en de traagheid van degene die je opvoedt
Het vermijden van veelvuldig verwijten
Het is belangrijk dat je, als man, geen «waarom»-vragen stelt tenzij je werkelijk de reden wilt weten achter wat iemand gedaan heeft. Dat doe je het beste nadat je de persoon in de juiste richting naar verbetering hebt gestuurd. Ik merk dat ik soms verwijtend denk (waarom heb je dat gedaan / niet gedaan).
Het vermijden van kwaadwillige vermoedens en het naspeuren van de gebreken van de betreffende persoon, dat wil zeggen het graven naar de fouten van de persoon.
Ik merk dat ik perfectie van de ander verwacht en dat die ander geen fout mag maken. Sinds de lessen van 3ilm shu-oon al-usrah (kennis van familieaangelegenheden) ben ik me hiervan meer bewust geworden en weet ik ook dat dat onrealistisch is. Daarnaast verwacht ik iets onmogelijks waarin ik zelf niet het goede voorbeeld kan geven (ook ik ben niet perfect en maak ook fouten). Als moslim behoor je voor de ander verontschuldigingen te zoeken en zeker te verwachten dat iemand een fout maakt. Dat valt onder het zesde punt (verwacht de fout en de traagheid van degene die je opvoedt).
Verwacht de fout en de traagheid van degene die je opvoedt
Waarom behoor je dat te verwachten? Ten eerste omdat het menselijk is. Ten tweede omdat zo'n persoon waarschijnlijk daaraan gewend is en ook tijd nodig heeft om te veranderen.
Ik kon de afgelopen week oefenen met het nichtje van mijn man [zijn verwante] van zes jaar oud. Toen ze bij ons was, was ze een beetje koppig. Sommige dingen liet ik passeren (ze wilde geen deken delen met haar andere nichtje, ze was volgens haar zeggen vaak boos of verdrietig), maar toen ze — spelend/lachend — druiven op de tafel gooide, merkte ik dat ik geïrriteerd raakte. Vooral omdat zij het zelf heel grappig vond. En ik merkte ook dat ik eigenlijk wilde vragen waarom ze dat deed. Niet omdat ik de reden wil weten, waardoor het een verwijt zou zijn. In plaats daarvan noemde ik (rustig) haar naam zodat ze op mij lette en zei ik dat ze niet met eten mocht gooien/spelen. Toen keek ze mij aan en zei «Sorry».
Ik heb uit de les de andere kant leren kennen, dat ik verkeerd/harder had kunnen reageren vanwege de irritatie die ik voelde, waardoor mijn nichtje koppig zou worden. Dat is niet gebeurd — en alle lof komt Allaah toe.
De leraar: Verwijten is dat je veelvuldig «waarom» vraagt op retorische wijze. Dat is wanneer je [iets impliciet] wilt zeggen.
Bespreking van studente 3
De zuster heeft de punten uitgeprint zodat ze die ook bij zich heeft. De zuster heeft de punten niet in de praktijk gebracht, vooral ook omdat ze naar haar gevoel niet echt in de positie van de opvoeder was. Daarom vond ze het moeilijk om ze op die manier te tonen. Ze dacht ook: als ze een les zou moeten geven, hoe zou ze daarmee kunnen omgaan.
Het vijfde punt (het vermijden van kwaadwillige vermoedens): [Er is] een zuster die altijd naar de lessen komt. Ze praat soms veel tijdens de lessen. Ze merkt van zichzelf dat ze dat altijd van haar verwacht. Ze denkt dan kwaadwillig, terwijl [dat] helemaal niet zo is. Daar heeft de zuster zichzelf betrapt vanwege dat punt, omdat ze er daarvoor niet over had nagedacht.
De leraar: Het kwaadwillige vermoeden over degene die je opvoedt is buitengewoon gevaarlijk en kan ook een averechts effect hebben in de opvoeding. De oorsprong ervan is het niet-goede vermoeden over Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa (verheven en geprezen is Hij). Dat lijkt een beetje ver weg, maar het is werkelijk zo. Wanneer je meer op Allaah vertrouwt, voor die [persoon] du3aa-e (smeekbede) doet en erop vertrouwt dat hij zichzelf zal verbeteren. Uiteraard heb je maatregelen nodig, maar je behoort erop te vertrouwen dat die [persoon] zichzelf verbetert. Als je er niet van uitgaat dat die [persoon] zichzelf verbetert, dan heeft dat ook dat effect. De Profeet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam zei: «أنا عند ظَنِّ عبدي بي». [«Ik ben zoals Mijn dienaar over Mij denkt».] En al zou het je meer moeite kosten, dan behoor je daarvan uit te gaan. Dat [is] het goede vermoeden in het algemeen en over degene die je opvoedt. En het is gebouwd op het goede vermoeden over Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa.
Bespreking van studente 4
Bij het tweede punt (de oprechte opvoeding) maar ook het achtste punt (alle deuren van verbetering en terugkeer naar Allaah open houden en ze nooit sluiten). Een verwante van een andere zuster had belangstelling voor de Islam. Vandaag was die zuster bij ons in de les. Bij haar was [het geval] dat ze de Islam omhelsd had omdat ze problemen had, en ze vond er rust in en vond het allemaal logisch. We legden haar uit dat het mooi is dat ze de Islam omhelst omdat ze er de Waarheid in ziet en dat Allaah de Enige is die het waard is aanbeden te worden.
De leraar: Welk opvoedkundig punt heb je toegepast?
De zuster: De punten 2 en 8, want we hadden gemakkelijk kunnen zeggen «ah mooi, welkom, natuurlijk is ze welkom», maar ook haar laten weten wat de Islam is en dat het belangrijk is dat die erkend wordt, dus daarom het tweede punt.
De leraar: Kwam ze als bekeerlinge [wie geleid is]?
De zuster: Ja, alleen leek het alsof [het] nog niet goed bezonken was, omdat ze veel problemen had doorstaan en rust in de Islam had gevonden.
Het achtste punt heb ik in de praktijk gebracht. Ze voerde een goed gesprek met haar kleine broer. Hij liet blijken dat hij geïnteresseerd is in zijn kennis en dat hij de Islam beter wil praktiseren, maar hij en zijn vrienden voelen een terugval omdat ze niet het gevoel hebben perfect te zijn. Bepaalde zonden zijn niet goed, maar de deur van berouw staat elke dag open als je terugkeert naar Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa.
De leraar: [Er is] nog een ander punt waaraan je hem kunt herinneren/waarmee je hem kunt vermanen. Het is niet alleen zo dat wanneer je berouw toont, je berouw aanvaard wordt, maar [er is] ook nog een ander punt.
Hij zei: «Wat mij tegenhoudt is dat we niet zo perfect zijn en veel zondigen». Is iemand van de mensen perfect? De perfectie van de mensen is dat ze fouten maken. Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa heeft ons zo geschapen dat we fouten maken. Dat wij in ons systeem ook fouten maken. En dat betekent dat je niet naar perfectie moet gaan zoeken, maar de perfectie is dat je berouw toont, niet dat je wacht tot je 100% bent, want die dag zal niet komen. 100% zijn [is] dat je elke keer berouw toont over je zonden, je zonden verafschuwt, en je zonden zoveel mogelijk wegwerkt.
Dit is een uiterst belangrijke vermaning die gegeven behoort te worden, zodat men niet wacht op een moment dat nooit zal komen.
sections.title_nl: Aanvulling op het oplossen van problemen
sections.content_en:
We dealt with the first definition of improving mistakes. And it has a connection with the behavior of the educator (murabbie) and his interaction with the behavior of the one being educated.
That one be truthful in education (that one have a truthful education)
When does the educator achieve a truthful education? That he educates for the sake of Allaah. There the truthful education begins: that one bases the education on [being] for the sake of Allaah. So the content of the education, the manner, the priorities, and the methodology of the education should be for the sake of Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa and should fall under the pleasure of Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa, because the personality of the educator and his intention have a direct effect on his education and on the success of his education, but also on the effect of the education on the one being educated.
And if we want to make it more concrete [tangible], it also has an effect on the trust between the two parties, which is also an essence in achieving this education. When the educator commits to a truthful education, it means that he does not correct except on the basis of the pleasure of Allaah, not on the basis of personal desires, and that ensures that the educator is at a level higher than the level of the one being educated, and it gives the educator awe and dignity, because the one being educated sees that his educator fears none but Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa and no one else.
That means that the educator should also keep away from vain talk or excessive laughter. He is permitted to joke, but he should not laugh excessively or display much behavior that harms his personality in the eyes of the one he educates, or display bad behavior, or carry out certain doubtful matters, so that his position is thereby lowered in the eyes of the one he educates.
We clarified previously that the one who educates (the educator) should have authority [prestige] and should radiate authority. When one carries out all these matters that are not good, then his authority will diminish or even disappear entirely.
And one should also not make light of the forbidden matters and say "this is merely a small sin, no problem." This too will bring the educator down to a lower position.
So the educator should also not occupy himself with vain matters. And the educator should also keep away from everything that he forbids the other from, and from lying too, so that trust and authority in the eyes of the one he educates remain forever.
Some examples of that: when one is educating and goes and starts with his personal issues and his personal feelings, such that the one he educates also sees whatever points of weakness he has and whatever tribulations (fitan) inflict harm on him. For example, the teacher of Islamic studies/weekend school sits with his pupil and goes and shares certain matters about her domestic situation; if it is a sister recounting that she is oppressed by her husband, and that she sees that her husband is lying, then she goes — for example — and recounts that she spies on her husband because she suspects that he is in contact with women.
Will such a pupil continue to respect such a teacher as before? No, you are clarifying your points of weakness. She cannot help you, and you should keep your points of weakness with yourself and ask someone of knowledge — and also not [someone] who is an equal to you, but rather [someone] who helps you. The one you need to educate you, you should not make yourself an equal to him or show yourself weaker toward him. That ensures that [there] no longer remains authority, and if the pupil sees that you have this point of weakness, then they do not see your weakness [your worth is lowered], or some of them exploit you, or other pupils tell about your points of weakness, such that your position falls in their eyes too. These are doors for the shaytaan.
Or when you, as a teacher, go and complain to your pupils about how the administration (the administration of the mosque or the school) treats you. That is one of the worst matters that bring the teacher down in the eyes of the pupil, no matter how the pupil responds. The pupil will not say "I no longer see you as a role model." At that moment the pupil will not say that; rather he will try to console you, to radiate a kind of affection, that he feels sorry for you, wanting to take your side. At that moment you have opened the doors of the shaytaan.
According to the position of such a pupil, the shaytaan goes and uses him either to lead you astray as a teacher, or as a tribulation (fitnah) for other teachers or other pupils.
Among the mistakes that the teacher encounters often is a mistake like this. That the teacher takes a weak stance, so the pupil no longer [reveres him], and the pupil goes and exploits him in a fitnah between several teachers or in a desire on the part of the pupil.
For example: a teacher said to a pupil who was working in the mosque, the weekend school: "It is not right, this mosque gives us very little money and I also have to pay my loan in Morocco." "How much do you have to pay in Morocco?" "I have many loans, I would like to finish building my house. The third floor in Morocco has been delayed very much. The mosque is a bit stingy."
How will such a pupil look at such a teacher? "He is smuggling into us [chopping up our education] to build his third floor in Morocco."
Question
On the weekend a sister gives Qur'aan lessons to sisters. She sometimes says in the lesson that she too sometimes finds it difficult to start memorizing the Qur'aan. Is this like it [like the previous mistake]?
At that moment you are discouraging them. It is not permissible to utter something like that, because you are saying "you actually have an excuse, because your teacher too has these moments, so you may have these moments too." You are the role model. You should rather set the example by saying: "Everyone has a moment in which he is active and a moment in which he is sluggish, but when one is sluggish one should remember the reward of Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa."
That is all [the difference between it] and saying to them "I go through that too sometimes." By that you make yourself a role model in such behavior.
This is one of the matters that the teacher is not permitted to carry out at all, for in that case one is discouraging the pupil instead of encouraging him. The teacher too has points of weakness, every human being has that, but one should encourage the other. That every human being has a point of weakness is a fact. Some people say "yes, everyone makes mistakes, you do not need to repeat that." Take care to improve yourself. Instead of saying "everyone makes mistakes" — that is one of the discouragements that the caller (daa3iyah) or the educator carries out.
Making use of recreational activities [play]
The educator is not only serious. Sometimes it is also important that you have a fitting joke or fitting recreation together or fitting play together that you also use for education. You use this to strengthen the bond and to firm it up, because you are interested in the other and you also see the other from another side. When one plays [is playful] one is warmer and releases more feelings than if one were serious and grave. At that moment you get to know such a person from another side.
You ensure that [between you and him] there is a firmer bond.
The Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam also had such a bond with 3aa-ishah. 3aa-ishah says in a hadieth that she narrated and that Imaam al-Albaanie declared authentic: «دَعاني النبيُّ صلَّى الله عليه وسلَّم إليه والعبيدُ السودُ يَلعَبون بحِرابهم في المسجدِ في يومِ عيد، فأقامَني خَلفَه وأَخفَضَ كَتِفَه حتى أَنظُرَ إليهم فنَظَرتُ من فوقِ كَتِفه» ("The Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam called me to him while the Abyssinians were playing with their spears in the mosque on the day of 3ied, so he stood me behind him and lowered his shoulder so that I could look at them, and I looked from over his shoulder") (then in the end she climbed onto his shoulder). So he said: «أَحَسبُكِ؟» [Is that enough for you?] She said: No, and he kept saying: "O 3aa-ishah, is that enough for you?" until I had had enough. And he sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam said: «قَدِّري حَقَّ البنياتِ الصغيراتِ في السِّنِّ اللاتي يُحبِبنَ اللَّعِب». ("Appreciate the right of the little girls, young in age, who love play"). That is, among the rights of children, especially girls, is that they play. That the educator should deal with and take into account.
And another hadieth that Imaam al-Bukhaarie also declared authentic, in which 3aa-ishah says: «قَدِمَ رسولُ اللهِ صلَّى الله عليه وسلَّم من غزوةِ تَبوكَ أو خَيبَر، فهَبَّت ريحٌ شديدةٌ كَشَفَت عددًا من بَناتِ عائشةَ [دُماها] التي كانت تَلعَبُ بها، فقال: ‹يا عائشةُ، ما هذا؟› قالت: ‹بَناتي›، ورأى بينها فَرَسًا له جَناحانِ من رِقاع، فقال: ‹ما هذا الذي بينها؟› قالت: ‹فَرَس›، قال: ‹وما هذا الذي عليه؟› قالت: ‹جَناحان›، قال: ‹فَرَسٌ له جَناحان؟› قالت: ‹أَما سَمِعتَ أنَّ لسُليمانَ فَرَسًا له أجنِحة؟› فضَحِكَ حتى بَدَتْ نَواجِذُه». ("The Messenger of Allaah sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam came from the expedition of Taboek or Khaybar, and a strong wind blew that uncovered a number of 3aa-ishah's dolls [her toys] with which she used to play, so he said: 'O 3aa-ishah, what is this?' She said: 'My dolls.' And he saw among them a horse with two wings of cloth, so he said: 'What is this that is among them?' She said: 'A horse.' He said: 'And what is this that is on it?' She said: 'Two wings.' He said: 'A horse with two wings?' She said: 'Have you not heard that Sulaymaan had a horse with wings?' So he laughed until his back teeth showed.")
That means that the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam took that into account in the education of his wife. Likewise, when the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam sent Anas ibn Maalik to fetch something for him. This hadieth was narrated by Imaam Aboe Daawoed and declared authentic by Imaam al-Albaanie. He said to him: "I will not go and fetch it," but in his head was "I will go and fetch it," so Anas set off and saw children playing (and he too was a child), so he became occupied and went on playing with them. Then the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam came and took him by the nape of his neck, so Anas looked behind and saw the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam smiling.
So you see that the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam took into consideration a child who is also tempted by play, and he did not reproach him. And in the end Anas knew what he should do, so he went and fetched it.
If this was the behavior of the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam — that he sometimes jokes with the one he educates, and laughs sometimes and is playful — then we should take that into account in our education. Especially regarding play with the wife and play with the children. Especially the man who plays with his wife. He carries out something that pleases Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa if he does it with a pure intention.
We dealt previously with the hadieth that every amusement and play is futile except three: «الرَّميُ، وتأديبُ [تَدريبُ] الفَرَس، ومُلاعَبةُ الرجلِ أهلَه». ("Archery, disciplining [training] the horse, and a man's playing with his wife"). Play with your wife, the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam says, is not futile play, because it is one of the essential, important matters that firm up the education, the communication and the bond between the man and his wife and his children. And that is why it is important that the man occupy himself with that too. Toward his wife firstly and toward his children. It will be good for the man to be cheerful. That has a direct effect on the relationship with the woman. And it will also be good for the woman to be cheerful toward the man, and for each of them to appreciate the other's humor. This is a blessing if you have it and attain it from Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa to improve the bond between the two spouses.
However, this matter should not be made a goal but merely a means. One should not exaggerate in play and recreation (such that it becomes a kind of goal, a daily occupation, such that they need only to laugh together, and if they do not do so they become depressed and sad), and on the other hand one should not engage in no play and recreation at all and think that when he plays with his wife and children his authority diminishes. That is incorrect, because alongside authority you also need love from the side of the one you educate. That love is also composed of play and recreation when you use them in a moderate measure.
Question: Anas said to the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam "I will not go and fetch it" — did he not thereby refuse a command?
The answer: He was a child of six or seven. He is the narrator of this narration. He said that he would not go and fetch it, but he went and fetched it. In this way you can understand children sometimes too. He was a child below buloegh (puberty), so he is not blamed.
Question: Disciplining the horse — is it from the Sunnah that you learn horse-riding, or disciplining the horse only?
The answer: [The matter] here is in the motive of the action, not the action itself. The motive is that you prepare your mount for riding; that you do nowadays by giving your car a major servicing, which serves as [that].
So it is not [the case] that you are encouraging horse-riding specifically?
No. Nowadays [the matter] is no longer encouraging horse-riding but rather encouraging driving the car. As for archery, you are encouraging archery itself. Disciplining the horse was encouraged for horse-riding, for djihaad in the path of Allaah. Does this mean that the woman should not ride the horse or shoot? Play and recreation among women already exist. The Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam often approaches matters with people who do nothing or do it too much. Example: when the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam says: «لَعَنَ اللهُ النامِصاتِ والمُتَنَمِّصاتِ، والواشِماتِ والمُستَوشِمات». ("Allaah has cursed the women who pluck eyebrows and those who have them plucked, and the women who tattoo and those who have themselves tattooed"). Men and women are cursed together, but these acts are especially common among women. When he wants to encourage something, he encourages matters that are scarce in that gender or common in that gender, but it is fundamentally a general matter.
Fencing: apart from the fact that you become skilled in handling the sword. Shooting with a pistol or other firearms.
Did the scholars decide this on the basis of analogy (qiyaas), so that fundamentally one starts from what the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam decided?
This is on the basis of analogy, because it is the motive. Archery itself does not mean that it is not good; horse-riding or disciplining the horse does not mean that it is not good. The Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam encouraged it at that time for djihaad and for duty. You do not have hunting by archery. [The matter] here is in the motive. A time will come in which we ride horses more, and shoot, and shoot arrows and spears, and we no longer have the possibility of using electronic things. The Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam spoke about that.
Avoiding excessive reproach
Anas ibn Maalik narrated: «خَدَمتُ رسولَ اللهِ صلَّى الله عليه وسلَّم عَشرَ سنينَ بالمدينةِ وأنا غُلام، ليس كلُّ أمري كما يَشتَهي صاحبي [أن أكون]، ما قال لي فيها أُفٍّ قَطُّ، ولا قال لي: لِمَ فَعَلتَ هذا؟ ولا: ألَّا فَعَلتَ هذا؟ كان رسولُ اللهِ صلَّى الله عليه وسلَّم أحسنَ الناسِ خُلُقًا. أَرسَلَني يومًا لحاجةٍ، فقلتُ: واللهِ لا أَذهَب، وفي نفسي أن أَذهَبَ إلى ما أَمَرَني به رسولُ الله. قال: فخَرَجتُ حتى أَمُرَّ على صِبيانٍ وهم يَلعَبونَ في السوق، فإذا رسولُ اللهِ صلَّى الله عليه وسلَّم قد قَبَضَ بقَفايَ من ورائي، فنَظَرتُ إليه وهو يَضحَكُ فقال: ‹يا أُنَيس، اذهَب حيثُ أَمَرتُك›، فقلتُ: نعم، أنا أَذهَبُ يا رسولَ الله». Interpretation of the meaning: «I served the Messenger of Allaah sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam for ten years in Madeenah while I was a boy, and not everything I did was as my companion wished [me to be]. He never once said "uff" to me, nor did he say to me: "Why did you do this?" nor: "Why did you not do this?" The Messenger of Allaah sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam was the best of people in character. One day he sent me on an errand, and I said: "By Allaah, I will not go" — though inwardly I intended to go and do what the Messenger of Allaah had commanded me. He said: So I went out until I passed by some boys who were playing in the market, and then suddenly the Messenger of Allaah sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam had taken hold of the back of my neck from behind me. I looked at him and he was laughing, and he said: 'O Unays, go where I commanded you.' I said: 'Yes, I am going, O Messenger of Allaah.'» By "his companion" he means the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam.
If you look here, you see that the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam did not rebuke Anas nor reproach him. [The matter] here concerns only reproach, and reproach nullifies much of the tarbiyah. It causes the one being raised to tend to defend himself and vindicate himself, such that a person also falls into the fitnah (trial) of lying.
When the educator delivers such reproach often and frequently begins with "why" as an opening for reproach, then the one being raised will also make a habit of defending himself. That is a bad trait.
And what is a worse trait still is that he tends toward lying. And lying is an even worse trait, and what is worse still is that he is not helped toward a solution and improvement.
This can also lead to friction between the educator and the one being raised, such that the one being raised rebels. So instead of going and causing all that harm as an educator, make sure that you drive the one you are raising toward the solution. Because that ensures that the one being raised is spurred toward what he ought to do, instead of remaining stuck in a vicious circle and clinging to that, even to his sin or his misdeed. In that case, as an educator, you are pushing such a person even further away from improvement.
That is why it is important, as a man, that you do not pose "why" questions unless you truly want to know the reason behind what a person did. That you do best after you have driven the person in the right direction toward improvement.
This does not apply only to the man toward his wife, but also to the woman, the mother toward her children. We will return to that later. And this also applies to communication from the husband, when the wife likewise poses such "why" questions, so that the husband, out of his weakness, is afraid to give his wife a truthful answer because otherwise she will shout, so he lies to her.
Such a case also came to the teacher. A man and a woman came to the teacher's office. Among the main reasons they had was that the woman used to complain a lot and, in reality, put the man down through her communication, because with her everything had a complaint in it. "I do not want you to do this, I ask you to do that, why do you not do that, why do you do this to me." So that in the end the man gave up and said, "I will lie then." So that the woman then says, "My husband lies a lot." So that the man admits that he lies because he is afraid of his wife.
Reproach should not be present in the relationship between the man and the woman; rather, make sure that you drive matters toward good, and spur, and admonish. In admonition there is no reproach.
Avoiding suspicion and following up the faults of the person concerned, that is, digging into a person's mistakes.
The Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam says in a hadieth which Imaam al-Albaanie graded authentic: «إنَّ الأميرَ إذا ابتَغى الرِّيبةَ في الناسِ أَفسَدَهم». Interpretation of the meaning: «Indeed, when the ruler seeks out suspicion among the people, he corrupts them.»
And he sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam said in another hadieth: «يا مَعشَرَ مَن آمَنَ بلسانه ولم يَدخُلِ الإيمانُ قلبَه، لا تُؤذوا المسلمين، ولا تَعِيبوهم [تُعَيِّروهم بفُروعهم]، ولا تَتَّبِعوا عَوراتهم (أي لا تَحفِروا عن سوءاتهم)، فإنَّه من تَتَبَّعَ عَورةَ أخيه المسلمِ تَتَبَّعَ اللهُ عَورتَه، ومن تَتَبَّعَ اللهُ عَورتَه فَضَحَه ولو في جَوفِ بيته». Interpretation of the meaning: «O company of those who have believed with their tongue while iemaan has not entered their heart, do not harm the Muslims, and do not disparage them [reproach them for their shortcomings], and do not follow up their faults (that is, do not dig into their misdeeds), for whoever follows up the fault of his Muslim brother, Allaah will follow up his fault, and whomever Allaah follows up his fault, He exposes him even in the depths of his house.»
Suspicion and digging into mistakes is destruction to the tarbiyah.
Suspicion is speculating about the other and expecting the worst from him. That is its practical meaning. Instead of doing that, you ought to expect the best from the other and seek excuses for him when he errs. When you do not do that, an atmosphere of doubt arises in the house, and it can lead to a large gap between the educator and the one being raised, such that the one being raised reacts against the educator, and continually feels attacked, or unappreciated, or untrusted, and that can lead to harm, such that in the end he says: "The one who is raising me does not trust me, so why should I make an effort to do good." That causes the destruction of the tarbiyah and also [the destruction of] the one being raised.
Following up someone's misdeed, digging into the misdeed, and spying, ensures that there is no trust between the two sides and that a person focuses only on the mistakes, instead of also using the good things and good qualities for the tarbiyah. Nor should a person mock another when he errs; that too causes these two effects, namely that the one being raised no longer respects the one raising him and that a gap arises, and, on top of that, that that [person] goes and behaves accordingly. That he goes and behaves according to those sins, that he makes them a habit.
Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa (glorified and exalted is He) will also punish that [person] by exposing him from his own house. What is more concealing than his own house? Almost nothing. And yet Allaah will punish him from his house. It is a great sin if the educator does that.
So do not go, as a man, constantly monitoring what your wife errs in. She made the bed but some wrinkles remained on the bed. She prepared food but the food is cooked a little too much or [has no] salt. She said a word wrongly without intending it.
Paying attention to such things destroys the tarbiyah. Such things you should not even see; you should not pay attention to them. Your focus should not be there.
Remember, as a man, that you also err a lot and your wife keeps silent about it too; that also creates love between the two of you. That can also create something good and positive between the two of you if you do not go paying attention to this matter.
So the man should not stop at every mistake, nor should the woman stop at every mistake. And nothing [is said] and no reminder is given except when a small sin is repeated a lot. And when a great sin occurs, only then should something be said about it; but at every mistake, or that you not content yourself with not paying attention to mistakes but go searching for mistakes — that is not permissible in Islam. Neither in tarbiyah nor between you and your brothers/sisters.
That is why the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam says: «إنَّ الأميرَ إذا ارتابَ في الناسِ أَفسَدَهم». Interpretation of the meaning: «Indeed, when the ruler harbours suspicion of the people, he corrupts them.»
And thus Islam made spying a great sin. Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa says in Soorat al-Hudjuraat: «ولا تَجَسَّسوا». Interpretation of the meaning: «And do not spy.»
Suspicion transforms a person into bad conduct, in both the man and the woman. The man should spur the woman positively at all times so that the bad thoughts are removed.
Expect mistakes and the sluggishness of the one you are raising
Why should you expect that? Firstly because it is a human matter. Secondly because such a person is most likely accustomed to it and also needs time to change.
When you do not expect that he will err, you will be one of two people: either you go, at that moment, trusting blindly that [the matter] is going well at that moment, and that causes slackness in the educator, such that you no longer follow up the one you are raising and look at whether he is doing well, so that he errs again a lot and continually stays in his bad habit. That again causes the discouragement of the educator, and can in the end also cause the discouragement of the one being raised.
The discouragement of the educator, because that [person] then says, "This person has failed, or I have failed, so I will no longer try and will not follow up the person."
And with the one being raised: "I have failed, so I cannot; I tried, so I cannot."
Whoever is a true leader does not do that. He keeps following up that [person], because when he is not doing well he can alert him directly toward the positive.
And there is another side to which [the matter] can lead, which is that a person becomes annoyed with this person who is being raised, so he goes and responds in a wrong way, in a harsher way, such that the person concerned who is being raised no longer wishes to be improved and so becomes obstinate.
So both directions, both consequences, are destruction to the tarbiyah. The Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam says in an authentic hadieth: «كلُّ بني آدمَ خَطَّاء». Interpretation of the meaning: «Every son of Aadam is a persistent sinner.» A persistent sinner [one who errs much]. He sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam did not say "they err," no, but they err continually, «وخيرُ الخَطَّائينَ التَّوَّابون». Interpretation of the meaning: «and the best of the persistent sinners are those who repent.» Make sure that you drive that person each time toward showing repentance.
The Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam says: «لكلِّ عملٍ شِرَّةٌ، ولكلِّ شِرَّةٍ فَترة، فمن كانت فَترتُه إلى سُنَّتي فقد اهتَدى، ومن كانت فَترتُه إلى غيرِ ذلك فقد هَلَك». Interpretation of the meaning: «For every deed there is a burst of zeal, and for every burst of zeal there is a slackening; so whoever's slackening is toward my Sunnah has been guided, and whoever's slackening is toward other than that has been ruined.» [Meaning: whoever directs his activity toward his goal or the nearness of his goal — that is the one you should expect much from; and whoever is pointed at with fingers — expect nothing from the likes of him.]
That is, a person who tries to reach toward the pleasure of Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa, and when he does not succeed, has at least tried. That is a person who will attain [his aim]; but a person who always wants to be perfect and ideal will not attain.
Every human being has his mistakes, and the one who is raising should also be patient in improving the mistakes, and should not give up quickly or [let] these mistakes provoke him.
When you expect the mistake, you should also plan how you will improve that [person] if he makes this mistake again. That ensures that the tarbiyah you deliver is then organized and driven in the right direction, because you thought about it; and when you go and act impulsively and do not think that such a person will make the same mistake, then you will inevitably err too, as an educator, and you will be more led by emotion and more impulsive in your behaviour than if you had expected the mistake.
You should also expect that such a person who is being raised is not always active at the same level of activity. That he can sometimes be sluggish, sometimes lazy. That you should expect. So you should then try, at that moment, to choose the better over the good, or the less bad over the bad, if the good is not possible.
We dealt with that before with various ahaadieth and various examples.
If you cannot reach your goal and achieve it with such a person, then make sure that the less bad is carried out over the bad. Repel the bad with the less bad. That ensures that closeness is created between the one raising and the one being raised. And that no distance is created between the man and the woman.
Not focusing on small matters, small mistakes, and concealing them
Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa says in Soorat an-Noor (19): «إنَّ الذينَ يُحِبُّونَ أن تَشيعَ الفاحشةُ في الذينَ آمَنوا لهم عذابٌ أليمٌ في الدنيا والآخرة، واللهُ يَعلَمُ وأنتم لا تَعلَمون». Interpretation of the meaning: «Indeed, those who love that immorality should be spread among those who have believed will have a painful punishment in this world and the Hereafter. And Allaah knows and you do not know.»
What is the connection of this aayah to concealing small matters and not focusing on small matters?
When a person focuses on those small matters, the focus will be placed on the misdeed, and when a person continually emphasizes this misdeed, then this misdeed will also remain a mark [a brand] on the person concerned, and this ensures that such a person actually becomes bad. This is a form of spreading the misdeed. When a person does not conceal such a person, then he will no longer be ashamed to commit such a mistake. That too is a spreading of the misdeed, because when he is not ashamed to commit such a mistake, then he will commit such a mistake among people too, and there you will have brought him to it. When he commits the mistake among people because of your incorrect treatment of him, you will have spread this among the people.
Spreading sins openly is a form of driving others to them, spreading the misdeed.
And it is also incorrect to bring out certain sins that do not occur in the family and that the people of the family do not know about. For example, your wife does not know of such a sin, so you go and talk about it because you want a pleasant evening and you have no other topic. In that case you would be committing a sin, because showing that sin teaches your wife to be tempted, or she may be tempted, to commit such a sin.
A person should be careful of what he says. That is why concealment is among the important matters in Islam.
And that is why one of the most destructive and hideous "treatments" is organizing a "talk [support] group" in which a person goes and talks about his experience with a certain sin. Because at that moment the feeling fades away (and that is exactly what these devils among mankind want) that such a thing is a sin and that one ought to be ashamed of it. That they also say. They say: "If you see that other people do it too, then it will be easier for you." That [is] the call to sins. That is why a person should be wary of the treatments of the disbelievers, and of whether they even have any good at all in their psychology or their psychiatry.
Question: Is it a great sin to introduce this sin [bring it in]?
Answer: Yes.
Question: Do you mean — for example — a talk group for alcohol addicts?
Answer: Yes, for example, or drug addicts, or rapists, or [perpetrators of] murder, or smoking. "How do you engage in smoking? I engage in this, and the other engages in that." They do that to break the taboo [the unspoken forbidden]. Everyone you hear saying "we want to break the taboo" — its meaning is that he is a devil calling to sins by making them no longer detested in people's hearts. That is among the matters that corrupt the 3aqiedah.
And the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam also says: «من سَتَرَ مسلمًا [أخاه] في الدنيا سَتَرَه اللهُ يومَ القيامة». Interpretation of the meaning: «Whoever conceals a Muslim [his brother] in this world, Allaah will conceal him on the Day of Resurrection.» This is a universal law (1+1=2). If you conceal your brother, Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa will conceal you in this world and the Hereafter, and if you do not conceal him, Allaah will expose you in this world and the Hereafter.
And this is also a command. The command is to conceal your brother in principle, and it is forbidden to display the mistakes of your brother or your sister. And sometimes you should not even discuss those mistakes with him. Because he is ashamed before you, and that in itself is enough.
So you see that many of the Muslims have also taken this filth from the disbelievers, in that they see modesty as something incorrect. So they say, "You should not be ashamed." No — you should be ashamed; modesty is good. Modesty adorns the person. The Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam says: «والحَياءُ شُعبةٌ من الإيمان». Interpretation of the meaning: «And modesty is a branch of iemaan.»
You will have drawn an image of this person [such that] others also tend to treat him in that way. And you will also have caused yourself to spread this sin that you talk about. So by that you too are an indirect caller to this sin. It is not in vain that the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam says that the worst of ribaa [the most usurious of usury] is that you violate the honour of your brother.
So the educator should know that he has a great responsibility.
A person should keep all the doors of improvement and returning to Allaah open, and never close them
Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa has kept the doors of repentance always open, except when a person is in the throes [of death] or when he sees the sun rise from the west, as the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam also said in a hadieth that Imaam al-Albaanie graded authentic: «إنَّ اللهَ يَقبَلُ توبةَ العبدِ ما لم يُغَرغِر». Interpretation of the meaning: «Indeed, Allaah accepts the repentance of the servant as long as he does not reach the death-rattle.» This matter ensures that the one being raised always knows that there [is] a way back. Instead of pushing him away, you would be drawing him toward Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa.
It is not permissible to discourage such a [person] from performing repentance.
Points 9 and 10 we will do next week, then we will also do the second definition together with the completion of improving mistakes.
Questions
Question: When you discover a mistake in someone and he does not know that you know it, then it is not permissible for you to discuss this mistake. Is that correct?
Answer: It is not permissible for you to break his modesty. You should then give a general, indirect admonition. For example: "Come, let us listen to this lecture," and in that lecture there is an admonition about that sin which he commits. Or that you send an article, or that you say: "[There are] some people who do such and such, and the likes of these should fear Allaah."
That modesty you should preserve, conceal it. It is good that he has modesty. And for the same reason you yourself may fall into such a situation and need someone to conceal you. Every Muslim needs concealment.
Question: You recently shared about the school [that is] in the media. What exactly is expected of the Muslim community, and is it important for us to know it?
Answer: Yes, the Muslim community is expected firstly to be attentive to the schemes of the devils among mankind and jinn. These begin with the intelligence agency [AIVD], and the school of the ministries which tells lies, all the way up to the person who calls himself prime minister, all the way to a person who calls himself "al-Furqaanie" and has committed major kufr several times. He said: "I am the one who mocks the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam and stands with these people" (he sided with "Charlie").
These people have a plan, which is to remove every aspect of education, and of good conduct, from Islam, and of the good from Holland, because they know that this has a good effect on the youth.
The second matter is that a person should support this school. That they alert the parents to respond, and that we join hands as Muslims to preserve such a school.
The question is no longer whether the school is trustworthy or not. The school is 100% trustworthy. They tell lies because people are averse to terrorism. These lies will in the end fall upon them. One of the journalists said to this person who calls himself prime minister: "You do not come with facts, you have no facts." And the intelligence agency also makes clear that they have no facts except that they do not agree with the school's vision. "Are you not afraid of being sued [for] running a defamation campaign?" We should spread [this] among ourselves as Muslims. Do not believe these people; make sure to support the school, to enrol in the school, for Amsterdam and Utrecht [together]. Do not take "al-Furqaanie" seriously. If anyone has a supplication, or has said "I am in a moment in which my du3aa-e is hoped to be answered," then let him supplicate for this school and for those who exert their effort in this school to preserve the education, and let him supplicate against every person who wants to remove this good. Concerning the school and also other Islamic institutions engaged in da3wah. We should ask Him more. He subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa is on our side. We should not fight one another as Muslims, but rather embrace one another so that we support Islam and the Muslims.
Among the important universal laws is that any person who supports what the disbeliever wants, [know] that he himself is untrustworthy, even if he stands in the mosque with a djilbaab and a long beard and sheds some tears in humility — such a person you may not trust. For example [so-and-so], and "al-Furqaanie," and [so-and-so], and [so-and-so], and you have more than that. People who pretend to be imams or trustworthy.
Why? Because such a person is a devil whom these people use only to slip in among the Muslims, and he wants to convince the Muslims to do misdeeds.
They are actually carrying out the schemes of [the enemies of Islam], and at this moment [the schemes of] the prime minister, but for the sake of position among the Muslims.
We should supplicate for these Islamic institutions and against everyone who wants to inflict something on these Islamic institutions.
It is important that we take [the matter] seriously, that the youth convince one another, and convince the parents. This defamation campaign began with [the institution] "al-Fitrah." Then they made a tour of all the mosques, then they want to strike at this school.
Question: Using certain terms such as the term "Salafiyyah" or "the Salafi manhadj." We learn that we have the 3aqiedah of the Sunnah. Today [there is] much confusion concerning those terms. Can you clarify?
Answer: Such a term has been smeared by the journalists but also by the Muslims. In reality there are two [extreme] parties. Journalists who do not know what Salafiyyah means, and Muslims who misuse Salafiyyah and perform deeds that have no connection to Salafiyyah but rather to crime and major sins. Their deeds have no connection to Salafiyyah. We should not distance ourselves from this name, because this name is in reality — almost — the content of our religion: following the Salaf. We should clarify to people what this matter means, that we follow the Sahaabah, we follow the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam, and, on top of that, we follow the Qur'aan in the manner in which we pray, and in the manner in which we buy and sell, and in the manner in which we behave; and that this is not a group or a gathering or a theory. Salafiyyah is Islam. There is no other Islam. It is called so because in it we follow the Sahaabah. We are distinguished by that, because all the other groups do not follow the Sahaabah (the people of takfier, the Tableegh, the Sufis, etc.).
One of the journalists asked the teacher about twelve or thirteen years ago: Are you a Salafi? He said: No, I am not the Salafi that is in your head. I am a Salafi who follows the Qur'aan and the explanation of the Prophet and the Sahaabah. I am not a person who blows people up or oppresses people. That [is] the Salafiyyah which they spread. They smear this matter in order to turn people away from Islam. If you look carefully at the hideous face of such people, and especially [the programme] "Da3wah of the Century." One of the people who [is] a presenter is "Tijs van den Brink" — when he went to conduct an interview with "Joram van Klaveren" [he said]: "How do you enter a religion that says if you leave this religion your head is cut off? How do you enter a religion that disavows 3Iesaa? How do you enter a religion that oppresses women?" He was engaged with his viewers in discouraging them from entering Islam. Even "Joram" used that for his da3wah by giving beautiful answers. We should get ahead of them in the correct da3wah, because Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa has given us this magnificent religion. We should be wary as much as possible not to be pushed further into a corner in which we are afraid to attribute ourselves to Salafiyyah. You do not need to boast of it, but call to its content. In that case [the matter] should be good.
Question: How is it with the Madaakhilah? Do they too follow the da3wah of Salafiyyah?
The teacher: These people want to follow Salafiyyah, but because they went to excess, they no longer, in many matters, follow the Sahaabah. They did exactly like the other groups. They said: "We want the manhadj of the people of the Sunnah." And it is built on the evidence. Then they said: "Everyone who declares our scholars to be innovators is not from the people of the Sunnah." "You should not adhere to one or two persons, so why do you go and compel us to adhere to one person?" Another group (the Mu3attilah) say: "We do not want to liken Allaah to people, because Allaah is higher than people. Therefore we say that Allaah has no name and no attributes." Allaah said that He has names and that He has attributes. They cannot see them as attributes, because otherwise they would liken Allaah to man. That is like the Madaakhilah. Because of their desire they wanted to distance themselves from misguidance, and so they fell into greater misguidance. They declare all the scholars to be innovators. In one of the reports of the intelligence agency they said that they should use this sect and support it materially [in cash], so that the rest become divided.
Question: The Madaakhilah — do we nevertheless acknowledge them as scholars?
Answer: This scholar too began this fitnah, and that is why this fitnah is called by that [name] [being attributed to him]. But to be honest and fair, this shaykh disavowed these people who behave in this way. It is better to call this sect the sect of tabdee3 (declaring others to be innovators) or excessiveness in the sect of tabdee3.
Question: Have you spoken with these people before?
Answer: Yes, of course.
