Zij volgt de lessen niet via de sociale media, maar zij gaf aan dat zij via Instagram en [vlog]-clips op YouTube er ook door wordt beïnvloed en dat die haar denkwijze beïnvloeden.
De leraar: Op religieus gebied of een ander gebied?
De zuster: Zusters die de hidjaab als een stuk mode zien. De hidjaab wordt dan op een bepaalde manier gepresenteerd. Dat beïnvloedt de denkwijze van mijn nicht, hoewel zij de juiste hidjaab draagt. Zij krijgt een zwakker geloof en misschien neigt zij ook naar zo'n stijl van kleding. Zij gaf aan of zij daar niet meer naar zou kunnen kijken. Zij wil graag het leven van deze mensen volgen.
De leraar: Het is verboden dat je daarnaar kijkt. Het is verboden in de Islam dat je de zonde ziet en dat je erin geïnteresseerd bent. En zeker wanneer je merkt dat je daardoor in je denken wordt beïnvloed. Dan ben je je bewust van het gevaar, en het is nog strenger verboden voor wie zich ervan bewust is. Jij bent in gevaar, en Allaah heeft gezegd: «ولا تَقرَبوا الزِّنا». Interpretatie van de betekenis: «En nadert de zinaa (ontucht) niet.» Dit is een definitie voor elke zonde. Alles wat je dichter bij een bepaalde zonde brengt, is verboden, ook al is het op zichzelf geen zonde. Wanneer het in het algemeen geen zonde is, maar jij weet dat het je zal beïnvloeden richting een zonde, dan is het voor jou verboden.
Er kwam een persoon naar imaam Ahmad en zei: is het toegestaan dat ik een mes draag? Hij zag dat hij boos was en dat zijn gezicht rood was. Hij zei: nee, dat is niet toegestaan. En er kwam een andere persoon en stelde dezelfde vraag, en die persoon leek kalm te zijn, dus zei hij: het is toegestaan. Wanneer je een mes draagt is er niets mis mee, je gebruikt het om te koken, terwijl het mes je tot een zonde kan leiden, dus is er in het dragen van het mes iets wat niet klopt.
De meeste mensen zijn niet ruimhartig [verdraagzaam] wanneer [de zaak] binnen de kring van de familie is, dus zijn ze een beetje verlegen. Jij hebt werkelijk [tussen jou en haar] een opvoedkundige band.
De zuster: Dat heb ik met meerdere vrouwelijke familieleden.
Vervolgens vroeg ik haar; zij is namelijk zojuist begonnen met leseenheden in de plaatselijke moskee (Moskee As-Salaam in Gouda [Gouda]). De eerste eenheid gaat over de grondbeginselen van het kennen van de Islam. Deze wordt onderwezen door [iemand] van [de Al-Yaqeen-stichting]. Door deze lessen ging zij zien dat de Islam bestaat uit veel zaken die in haar gedachten waren. En haar vriendinnen heeft zij ook opgetrommeld [uitgenodigd] voor wat zij die vrijdag heeft geleerd, en zij maakt hen ook enthousiast om zich in te schrijven voor de volgende lessen.
Bij de tweede stap gaf de zuster haar aan — bij het deel waar zij door YouTube wordt beïnvloed — dat zij de isti3aadhah (het zoeken van toevlucht bij Allaah) zou moeten verrichten wanneer zij ertoe neigt hen te volgen. En zij had gezegd dat zij zich moet verwijderen van die website.
De leraar: Dat behoort al tot stap nul (bij de waarneming). Dat zij zulke waarnemingen niet meer zou moeten hebben, en dat zij Instagram stopzet behalve voor de vermaningen of de websites waarop vermaningen worden gegeven. De sociale media blijven een hevige verleiding. Daarin zit letterlijk elke soort vuiligheid. Zulke media zouden eigenlijk helemaal niet gebruikt moeten worden. Tot de zaken die de leraar de broeders en zusters heeft aangeraden bij [de les over] gezinsaangelegenheden op woensdag: zet de sociale media stop, want die zijn niets anders dan verleidend tot beproevingen, seksuele beproevingen, en valse berichten, en roddel. Ze vullen je leven met het kwade en met verderf, en daarmee vullen ze ook je hart en je hoofd ermee.
De leraar gaat niet meer op Facebook, behalve als hij een bericht [advertentie] wil plaatsen; hij plaatst het en gaat er weer uit.
Het is belangrijk om Facebook en YouTube volledig te verwijderen. Bij YouTube heb je ook een andere mogelijkheid, en dat is een betaalde app die "youtuzz" [youtuzz] heet. Deze app vul je met jouw afspeellijsten en de kanalen die je wilt, en dan kun je daaruit selecteren. Je kunt een bestand, een programma, importeren, en naargelang wat je op dat bestand hebt gezet kun je die video bekijken zonder advertenties en zonder verwijzingen. Dit gebruikt de leraar thuis voor de kinderen.
YouTube zelf heeft een nieuwe versie, maar je zou heel technisch moeten zijn om die in te stellen.
Je hebt ook andere programma's. Als je het kunt instellen, stel het dan in, en anders, gebruik de sociale media zo min mogelijk of [gebruik ze] helemaal niet, behalve — bijvoorbeeld — WhatsApp of een chatprogramma waarmee je met de mensen kunt praten. En los van dit advies, als zij lid is van iets, lid van een [Facebook-pagina] die zulke [inhoud] plaatst, dan zou zij zich daarvan moeten verwijderen. Dat is een islamitische verplichting. Het gevaar van de sociale media reikt veel verder. Voor elke "like" [waardering] word je bij Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa ter verantwoording geroepen. Want met de waardering heb je anderen daartoe aangezet. Je hebt andere mensen ertoe aangezet om te zien wat jij hebt gezien, zelfs van het kwade. Dus het is heel gevaarlijk.
De zuster: En ten slotte had de zuster met haar nicht besproken dat zij wat er in de wereld gebeurt gruwelijk vindt. Na die aanslagen in Nieuw-Zeeland gaf zij aan dat zij dieper in het geloof ging graven en er meer over ging nadenken. En vooral de Dag der Opstanding, dat heeft haar geloof vergroot.
De leraar: Zag je ook bepaalde ingevingen bij haar woorden en gaf je aan dat zij daarvoor op haar hoede moet zijn en dat deze wijze van spreken voortkomt uit datgene waardoor zij is beïnvloed? Het is belangrijk dat men nagaat wat men uitspreekt en wat de vrouw tot de zonde kan leiden.
De zuster: Zij gaf aan dat zij had opgemerkt — wanneer zij bepaalde clips op YouTube ziet — dat zij bang is dat zij erdoor wordt beïnvloed. Dan onderving zij de ingeving om die te negeren en zich van de website/YouTube te verwijderen.
De leraar: Het zou goed zijn dat je haar de rest van de adviezen geeft.
Bespreking van studente 2
De zuster voerde de huiswerktaak met zichzelf uit, omdat zij niemand had [met wie zij] een opvoedkundige band had. Zij keek naar zichzelf en voerde het huiswerk met zichzelf uit. Zij ging voor zichzelf na welke zonde zij begaat, en zij maakte een lijst, en wat de prioriteit daarin is en wat zij als eerste zou moeten behandelen. Er kwam één zaak naar voren die de voornaamste is, en dat is dat er in bepaalde situaties negatieve gedachten bij haar opkomen. Het zijn geen negatieve gedachten over anderen, maar ze betreffen haarzelf. Zij dacht na over waar ze vandaan komen, maar zij weet het niet, behalve dat zij zich er heel erg bewust van is. Sinds een tijd, en dat zij zichzelf betrapt dat het een negatieve gedachte is en waarom je die hebt. En ook dat het een gedachte is die niet klopt; dan verricht zij ook berouw en bidt zij om die gevoelens uit haar hart weg te nemen. [Er zijn] bepaalde situaties waarin die opkomen en zij die opmerkt, en het zijn geen situaties die zij kan vermijden, omdat het gewone dagelijkse situaties zijn. Het vermijden van die plaatsen vond zij moeilijk.
De leraar: Heb je niet nagedacht over de oorsprong van deze gedachten?
De zuster: Jawel, maar zij kon daarin niet tot iets komen. Zij bleef staan bij waar ze vandaan komen, maar zij heeft geen idee waar ze vandaan komen. Dat vond zij moeilijk. Zij ging na of er bepaalde uitspraken worden gedaan die daartoe leiden, en dat was [het geval]. Die uitspraken worden gedaan door anderen, niet door haarzelf, dus kon zij ze van die kant niet vermijden. Het zijn negatieve gedachten over haarzelf.
De leraar: Het zou goed zijn dat je dit nagaat bij iemand met kennis die je hierop antwoord geeft.
De zuster: Zij dacht na over hoe zij dit kan oplossen. Zij bleef bewust om zichzelf in de gaten te houden en de stappen in haar gedachten te houden.
De zuster ging bij zichzelf na hoe zij dit kan oplossen, en dat deed zij door middel van het denkschema, door bewust te blijven en zichzelf in de gaten te houden.
[Er is] een bepaalde waarneming die uit haar omgeving komt waardoor de ingeving bij haar komt, en dat is de negatieve gedachte die aanhoudt, en die gedachte klopt niet.
De leraar: Heb je niet nagedacht over de waarneming die je op dat moment hebt?
De zuster: Jawel, maar het zijn meestal bepaalde situaties die zich voordoen en die zij opmerkt. Waarnemingen van dagelijkse situaties. Niet bij iets bepaalds. Zij verrichtte veel berouw en blijft die du3aa-e verrichten in de neerknieling en op andere momenten. De gedachte hangt af van het geloof. Zij zou meer aan haar geloof moeten werken, opdat die negatieve gedachte niet opkomt. Dat deed zij. Zij dacht veel na over de grootsheid van Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa, en het zien van de tekenen van Allaah, en wat ook hielp was het reciteren van de Qur'aan in de ochtend na de fadjr. Wanneer zij die verzen reciteerde, [overviel haar] een verwondering die zij voelde. Die daalde rechtstreeks in haar hart neer en veroorzaakte veel khushoe3 tegenover Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa, en dat hielp tegen de negativiteit gedurende de dag. Zij merkte dat hoe meer zij dat deed, hoe beter [het was].
En tot wat zij ook deed, behoorde dat zij een cursus in het wassen van de doden heeft gevolgd. Dat was een zeer goede herinnering, en er was ook de mogelijkheid dat men in een lijkwade werd gewikkeld en in een kist ging liggen die daadwerkelijk werd gesloten. Zij koos ervoor dat te doen, omdat zij ermee [met de dood] geconfronteerd wilde worden. Sinds zij dat heeft gedaan, is het werkelijk een enorm verschil.
De leraar: Niet voor niets zegt de Profeet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam: «اذكُروا هاذِمَ اللذَّاتِ ومُفَرِّقَ الجماعات». [«Gedenkt de vernietiger van de geneugten en de verstrooier van de gezelschappen [de dood].»] Gedenk de dood veelvuldig, opdat men weet dat men hier slechts voor een korte tijd is en niet voor eeuwig, opdat men op de Dag der Opstanding wordt afgewend van het Vuur. Wanneer je de dood gedenkt, weet je dat je hier slechts voor een korte tijd bent. Je weet nooit wanneer de dood je treft. En de andere zuster zei dat haar nicht werd beïnvloed doordat zij meer ging nadenken over het vergaren van kennis vanwege de gebeurtenissen/aanslagen in Nieuw-Zeeland.
De leraar:
Van Soerat al-Ahqaaf tot Soerat an-Naas is wat als eerste op de Profeet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam werd neergezonden. Deze soerahs zijn ook voor het vergroten van het geloof, waarbij men de grootsheid van Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa kan verkennen.
Bespreking van studente 3
De zuster besprak het huiswerk met haar echtgenoot. Zij dachten samen na over het doel van het huiswerk.
Het doel: Dat zij niet over de zonde gaat nadenken, of dat hij bij haar niet zelfs maar een ingeving veroorzaakt die zo'n zonde wakker maakt.
Vervolgens bepaalden wij de prioriteiten naar de zwaarte van de zonde/fout. Het benoemen van de verleiding en de ingeving en de gedragingen die tot de zonde/fout leiden, was daarvan het moeilijkst. Wij maakten een tabel met zes vakken [kolommen]: de zonden/fouten, de prioriteiten, de verleiding, de ingeving, de gedragingen, en de oplossing.
De afgelopen week waren wij gericht op de zonde/fout die de eerste prioriteit had gekregen. Ik merk dat die is verbeterd. De zonde vindt minder plaats, maar is nog niet volledig weggenomen. Ik denk dat dit meer tijd nodig heeft. Wij denken dat het door het gebrek aan geloof komt.
De leraar: "Gebrek aan geloof" is heel algemeen. Het kan [zo] zijn vanwege verschillende soorten verleidingen die door elkaar heen gemengd zijn, of dat je op dat moment niets hebt gepland om te doen, waardoor je desondanks in verleiding wordt gebracht, of dat er iemand in je omgeving is die je tot deze zaak leidt zonder zich daarvan bewust te zijn, omdat hij over een bepaald onderwerp praat. Het kan van alles zijn. Je zou op een concrete manier moeten zoeken naar datgene wat je in verleiding brengt, want de shaytaan gebruikt het altijd om je in verleiding te brengen. Het hoeft niet één ding te zijn, maar het kan van alles zijn.
Je zou op je hoede moeten zijn voor deze zaken die wij in ons dagelijks leven doen, want de shaytaan leidt ertoe en onze zielen brengen ons ertoe. Wanneer wij op onze hoede daarvoor zijn, zouden wij de zaken die ons in verleiding brengen niet moeten naderen, want wanneer wij die naderen, worden wij naar binnen getrokken. De Profeet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam zei over het rechte pad: hij trok een rechte lijn, en aan beide zijden muren, en bij elke muur deuren waarover gordijnen hangen. En boven deze weg [is er] iemand die tegen de bewandelaar van deze weg zegt: "Wijk niet af, want wanneer je één van deze gordijnen opzij schuift, word je naar binnen getrokken." Deze muren zijn de grenzen van Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa — zegt de Profeet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam — en de deuren zijn de deuren van het verbodene, en de gordijnen zijn datgene wat de mens in verleiding brengt. Het zijn geen gesloten deuren.
Elk verbod is een deur waarover een gordijn hangt; je bent nieuwsgierig wat erachter is, waardoor je naar binnen wordt getrokken. Je zou zelfs niet moeten denken aan het nemen van zo'n afslag, maar recht vooruit lopen. Je zou moeten kijken wat je in verleiding brengt, om naar die afslag te kijken. Wat je daartoe in verleiding brengt, zou je moeten vinden en vermijden. Als je dit met jezelf doet, zal het gemakkelijk gaan met je kind. En wanneer je echtgenoot dit met jou doet, weet jij hem ook beter te begrijpen. Je zou het met hem moeten bespreken. "Het praten over een bepaald onderwerp brengt mij in verleiding tot een gedachte, en die gedachte brengt mij tot een zonde." Dan weet je echtgenoot om niet [te praten] over dat onderwerp.
Bespreking van studente 4
De zuster kan meer geduld hebben en langzamer boos worden. En de wegen daartoe: zij merkt dat het heel erg helpt om de Qur'aan in de ochtend na de fadjr te reciteren, en vooral uit Soerat al-Ahqaaf, en om de adhkaar te blijven verrichten, en wanneer zij een zaak heeft, die aan de leraar voor te leggen. Zij geeft aan dat er een bepaalde rust bij haar komt om met minder emotie op de situaties te reageren.
Vervolg van de vorige les
Elke goede daad die je geloof versterkt, is een zaak die tot de langetermijnoplossing behoort en die een uiterst belangrijk fundament vormt voor het verbeteren van de fouten. [Er zijn] twee verschillende soorten daden:
Daden die je dagelijks kunt verrichten.
Daden die aan de tijd gebonden zijn.
Zoals het gaan naar de moskee, het siyaam, de Hadj, en andere daden die aan de tijd gebonden zijn.
De goede opvoeder gebruikt alle mogelijkheden op dat moment aangaande de dagelijkse daden. Het is belangrijk dat de opvoeder een soort schema voor zichzelf heeft waarin hij kan zien in welke tijd hij zich bevindt, welke islamitische datum, en welke vormen van 3ibaadah (aanbidding) daaraan verbonden zijn. Bijvoorbeeld: wanneer men zich in [Dhoe] al-Hidjdjah bevindt, dan zijn de eerste tien [dagen] de belangrijkste dagen waarin je goede daden kunt verrichten en waarin je kunt vasten. 3aashoeraa-e, en de dag van 3arafah, en wanneer [het] betrekking heeft op de drie witte dagen (al-ayyaam al-biedh), enzovoort.
Je zou eigenlijk als Muslim een jaarschema moeten hebben waarin je kunt weten op welk [tijdstip] ik mij bevind (in welke tijd ik mij bevind) en hoe ik kan profiteren van de tijd waarin ik mij bevind. Dat is uiterst belangrijk.
Taak [opdracht]
Wie kan een soort schema maken waarin bepaalde daden staan die afhankelijk zijn van de tijd, dat wil zeggen afhankelijk van de islamitische datum. Een soort kalender (het hoeft niet per se een kalender te zijn), bijvoorbeeld in de maand Safar, in de maand ..., en dan voor elke maand daden die in de Sunnah zijn overgeleverd die [erin] kunnen plaatsvinden.
<< Saliema, en Nawaal, en Ming. Zij organiseren het en sturen het. Vergeet de zuivere intentie hierin niet.
Vraag over de taak
Heb je een betrouwbare website waarop ahaadieth over de maanden staan?
Islamway.com، islamweb.net، islaamqa، alaluka (een groene website [al-Aloekah]).
sections.title_nl: Vervolg van het oplossen van problemen
sections.content_en:
We are still looking at how we discuss/treat the first definition, and it concerns the behaviour of the educator toward the one he educates.
That one be sincere in the tarbiyah (that one has a sincere tarbiyah: that is, that one educates for the sake of Allaah).
Making use of enjoyable activities.
Avoiding excessive reproach.
Avoiding evil assumption and pursuing the faults of the person concerned, that is, digging up the person's mistakes.
Expecting the mistake and the sluggishness of the one you educate.
Not focusing on small matters, small mistakes, and covering them.
One should keep all the doors of improvement and returning to Allaah open and never close them.
We stopped at the ninth point.
The admonition and the tarbiyah should be delivered at intervals [with spacing]
And the meaning of that is that the educator should not be admonishing continuously or educating continuously. That is how the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam dealt with this matter. In a hadieth narrated by Imaam al-Bukhaarie, the son [of a man from Banoe] Salimah said: 3abdullaah ibn Mas3oed used to remind us once every Thursday, so a man said to him: "O Aboe 3abdir-Rahmaan, I would love that you remind us every day." So he said: «إنَّ الذي يَمنَعُني من ذلك أنِّي أَكرَهُ أن أُمِلَّكم، وإنِّي أَتَخَوَّلُكم بالموعظةِ كما كان النبيُّ صلَّى الله عليه وسلَّم يَتَخَوَّلُنا بها مخافةَ السَّآمةِ علينا». "Indeed, what prevents me from that is that I dislike wearying you, and I take care of you with the admonition just as the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam used to take care of us with it, for fear of boredom upon us."
So you see that not focusing on the admonition only, with permanent continuity, is one of the important educational means that can perpetuate the tarbiyah and help make it succeed. And it is part of man's fitrah (natural disposition) that when you say something very much to a person, he will grow weary.
If he were admonished every day, he would no longer yearn for the admonition; rather he would find that admonition boring, and that is not a correct way of tarbiyah. It contradicts the Sunnah of the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam.
And the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam also says: «كان رجلٌ من بني إسرائيلَ له أخ، كان أحدُهما مُذنِبًا والآخرُ مُجتَهِدٌ في العبادة. كان المُجتَهِدُ كلَّما رأى المُذنِبَ قال له: أَقصِر. فوَجَدَه يومًا على ذنبٍ فقال له: أَقصِر. فقال: خَلِّني وربِّي، أَبُعِثتَ عليَّ رقيبًا؟ فقال: واللهِ لا يَغفِرُ اللهُ لك». "There was a man from Banoe Israa-iel who had a brother. One of them was a sinner and the other was diligent in worship. Whenever the diligent one saw the sinner, he would say to him: Desist. Then one day he found him at a sin and said to him: Desist. He said: Leave me and my Lord, have you been sent as a watcher over me? He said: By Allaah, Allaah will not forgive you." In that moment Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa became angry with this diligent one and said: "Who is the one who swears by Me [who swears about My decree]?"
And at the end of the hadieth the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam says that Allaah enters the diligent one into the Fire and forgives the other (the sinner) and enters him into Paradise.
Whoever says to people "Allaah will never forgive you" has said something that is in the hand of Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa alone. No one has knowledge of the unseen, and no one informs Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa whether He forgives someone or not. So you see that focusing on the sin only wearies the person in the end. The Muslim also has good qualities. These good qualities you should approach and emphasise and mention, so that thereby an opportunity is created for the improvement of the sinner. If you focus on that only, then you will emphasise a negative time, and that distances the person from returning to Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa.
So it is very important that there be intervals. Intervals in which one also emphasises different, positive, good qualities of that [person], so that the other does not grow weary of being admonished. This does not apply to teaching only; rather it also applies to improvement, that it not happen daily and with the same focus and with the same method, without the method being changed, without the words being changed, for that causes weariness and places a wall between the educator and the one who is educated.
In the end the aim is that improvement happens and that one listens with his heart so that he becomes convinced and loves good and hates evil. Because when one does not listen with his heart, he will not improve and will not become convinced, and therefore Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa also says in Soerat Qaaf (37): «إنَّ في ذلك لَذِكرى لمن كان له قَلبٌ أو أَلقى السَّمعَ وهو شَهيد». Interpretation of the meaning: «Indeed in that is a reminder for whoever has a heart or lends an ear while he is a witness.»
The least that should be present in the admonition is that one listens with focus, and the highest presence is that he is also present with his heart. Then you also need intervals so that one does not grow weary.
It is very important that one teach and admonish before he reproaches and before he rebukes
We know the hadieth of the bedouin (who enters the mosque and urinates in the corner). The Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam prevented the Companions, not [the bedouin]. After he prevented the Companions, he let him urinate. What did he say to the Companions? «دَعوه ولا تُزرِموه». "Leave him and do not interrupt him." And he said to him: «إنَّما بُعِثتُم مُيَسِّرينَ ولم تُبعَثوا مُعَسِّرين». "You were only sent to make things easy and you were not sent to make things difficult." Then he taught him, because he was ignorant. He did not know how to distinguish between the inside of the mosque and its outside.
As a bedouin you could not distinguish much. And the meaning of that is that it is not permissible to reproach anyone or to rebuke him or even to admonish him before he learns, so he should be taught.
The first step of the steps of tarbiyah: teaching, then reminding, then repetition, then admonition, then reproach [rebuke], then punishment.
It is not permissible that you move from step 1 to step 4 or from step 1 to step 5 (punishment directly). It is important that you review these steps well and practise them.
And also in a hadieth narrated by Mu3aawiyah [ibn al-Hakam]. He said: «بينما أنا أُصَلِّي مع النبيِّ صلَّى الله عليه وسلَّم إذ عَطَسَ رجلٌ من القوم، فقلتُ: يَرحَمُك الله. فرَماني القومُ بأبصارهم، فقلتُ: واثُكلَ أُمِّياه، ما شأنُكم تَنظُرونَ إليَّ؟ فجَعَلوا يَضرِبونَ بأيديهم على أفخاذهم، فلمَّا رأَيتُهم يُصَمِّتونَني [سَكَتُّ]». "While I was praying with the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam, a man from the people sneezed, so I said: May Allaah have mercy on you. So the people threw their glances at me, so I said: May my mother be bereaved of me, what is the matter with you that you look at me? So they began to strike their hands on their thighs, and when I saw them silencing me [I fell silent]." So when the Messenger of Allaah sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam completed his prayer — may my father and my mother be his ransom (and it is an expression meaning that he is far dearer to him than his father or his mother) — he said: «ما رأَيتُ مُعَلِّمًا قَبلَه ولا بَعدَه أحسنَ تعليمًا منه. ما كَهَرَني [ما عَنَّفَني] ولا ضَرَبَني ولا شَتَمَني. قال: إنَّ هذه الصلاةَ لا يَصلُحُ فيها شيءٌ من كلامِ الناس، إنَّما هو التسبيحُ والتكبيرُ وقراءةُ القرآن». "I have not seen a teacher before him or after him better in teaching than him. He did not scold me [did not rebuke me], nor did he strike me, nor did he insult me. He said: Indeed this prayer, nothing of the speech of the people is fitting in it; it is only the tasbieh and the takbier and the recitation of the Qur'aan."
If you look at this incident that took place in the time of the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam, you see that the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam took into account that such a person does not have knowledge. Such a person had returned from the land [the desert] in which he was, and when he returned, the prayer was being refined in its rulings. Originally it was permissible for them in the prayer to speak and to eat and to drink. Then it was no longer permissible for them to eat and drink, then it was no longer permissible for them to come to the prayer while drunk, then speaking in the prayer was forbidden. The Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam took that into account. So you see that he was the best teacher and the best educator. He also took into account the state of the people.
So it is important that the educator not go provoking the one he educates or deliberately inflame his bad feelings or agitate him or deliberately try to make him obstinate (that the educator makes the one he educates obstinate) or deliberately give him something that pains him, and this pain would also be under a punishment that will not help him but rather will help toward the opposite of what is intended. For harshness before the need calls for it will work toward the opposite of what is intended. And harshness at the time of teaching and at the time of admonition and at the time of reminding will lead only to evil. Some people go even further. They go mocking the one they educate, by ridiculing him or sharing an image of derision, or even being sarcastic toward him or deriding him. All of this is an incorrect way and an incorrect treatment of the person concerned who is being educated. Therefore it is important that the educator guard his behaviour in this, and that he remind before he admonishes, and teach before he reminds, and admonish before he rebukes, and rebuke before he punishes.
In this Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa also placed a clear definition [rule] in the Qur'aan. Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa says: «ادفَع بالتي هي أحسن»، Interpretation of the meaning: «Repel by that which is better», that is, repel with the better.
Anger at the major sins
Anger here does not mean the mere showing of anger, but rather true anger from your heart at the major sins, concerning those who have passed the age of buloegh (puberty/maturity).
Concerning the partner: it is not correct that you laugh together or make light of [the matter] when major sins are actually committed. When do you distinguish between measured anger for the sake of Allaah because of the sin and anger for the sake of Allaah at the person?
When the person knows that it is a sin and is reminded that it is a major sin but keeps continuing, then it is important that one show anger, and also when he admonishes. However, anger at the person during the admonition is a little less than [the anger during] the rebuke, and during the punishment there is much more anger. This anger should be led by the Islamic legislation. But when one commits a major sin while he has no knowledge of it, is it permissible that you become angry at the person himself? No.
That is exactly like the two previous ahaadieth. But you become angry because of the major sin itself. So you should restrain yourself [with the awareness] that this matter is incorrect and that this matter should be improved. And do not become angry at him except when you know 100% that this person committed a major sin deliberately.
Another issue: someone comes to you and says "I committed a major sin, how do I correct myself?" Do you then go and become angry at him? No, he wants to improve himself. If you go and become severely angry, that may turn him away from improvement. Do not become angry except when that [person] refuses to improve himself.
The Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam informs about a village to which the angels of punishment were sent, so they said to Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa: «يا ربِّ، فيها عبدٌ لك يَعبُدُك ليلًا ونهارًا». "O Lord, in it is a servant of Yours who worships You night and day." So He said: «ابدَؤوا به، فإنَّه لم يَتَمَعَّر [يَتَغَيَّر] وجهُه فيَّ قَطُّ». "Begin with him, for his face never changed [altered] for My sake."
What is the meaning of that? When Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa sends the angels of punishment to a village, then its meaning is that they not only wrong [others] but also that they do not admonish one another, and do not improve one another. The universal way [of Allaah] is that Allaah does not punish a whole family or household when some of them warn one another. Rather [He punishes] one single person. When they do not warn one another, all the people will be punished, the righteous and the evil together. The righteous one does not want to fall into the evil soul at the evil one [that the evil one hate him], that is, he does not want to admonish them.
Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa says in the Qur'aan (Soerat al-Maa-idah: 78): «لُعِنَ الذينَ كَفَروا من بني إسرائيلَ على لسانِ داودَ وعيسى ابنِ مريم، ذلك بما عَصَوا وكانوا يَعتَدون». Interpretation of the meaning: «Cursed were those who disbelieved among Banoe Israa-iel by the tongue of Daawoed and 3iesaa the son of Maryam; that was because they disobeyed and were transgressing.»
79 — «كانوا لا يَتَناهَونَ عن مُنكَرٍ فَعَلوه». Interpretation of the meaning: «They used not to forbid one another from a wrong that they did.»
So anger for the sake of Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa is an obligatory matter and is also among the methods that Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa loves; rather He made it obligatory in the correct situation, and it also falls under the Sunnah of the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam. We see this recurring also in the Sunnah of the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam, like the hadieth in which some of the Companions were on a journey, and a wound struck one of them in his head, so he asked his companions whether they saw fit for him to perform tayammum instead of the ghusl, and they answered him that he should perform ghusl because he was in a state of djanaabah and that it is not permissible for him to perform tayammum. So this Companion died because of the ghusl. When they returned from the journey and asked the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam as they always used to do, the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam said: «قَتَلوه، قَتَلَهم الله». "They killed him, may Allaah kill them." So the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam not only became angry at them, but also supplicated against them. So you see that among the qualities of the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam is also that he used to become angry when the limits were transgressed.
Today the major sins are no longer called major sins. Even among the practising brothers and sisters, they then say "you should not take [the matter] with such magnitude, you should not speak with big words" (lying, deception, a major sin). In their hearts the major sin is belittled. This is a sign of belittling the major sins.
When you hear someone speaking about a major sin and he says "you should not speak with such magnitude, you should not take [the matter] with such narrowness, you should not speak with big words, here he comes again with his big words", then its meaning is that these people are sick in their hearts and that in their hearts they belittle the major sins and make them insignificant. This is a great danger.
When you belittle the sin, then it will have a reverse effect on the one who is educated. We should not belittle the major sins, nor belittle persistence upon a sin, because that too is a major sin. We should become angry at that under the conditions and situations that we just discussed.
And among the conditions is a hadieth narrated by Imaam Muslim, when Usaamah ibn Zayd killed a man after this man saw his sword in a battle and said "Laa ilaaha illa-llaah". Usaamah wanted to kill him and raised his sword against him. So that man said: "Laa ilaaha illa-llaah", so Usaamah killed him. He went to the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam. The Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam said: «أَقَتَلتَه؟» "Did you kill him?" So Usaamah said: Yes, but he was afraid of my sword. So the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam said: «أَشَقَقتَ عن قلبه؟ أَقَتَلتَه بعد أن قال لا إله إلَّا الله؟» "Did you split open his heart? Did you kill him after he said Laa ilaaha illa-llaah?" He kept repeating it (Did you kill him after he said Laa ilaaha illa-llaah?). He kept repeating it until Usaamah wished that he had not become Muslim except after that [that is, he wished that his Islam had been after this incident so that what he did would be erased from him]. This is how the Companions dealt with their sins when they regretted, because he knew that he had thereby committed one of the greatest of the major sins. And the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam paid the diyah (a kind of compensation, the money for the slain one, the blood-money) to the family of that [man]. And it was one hundred camels, and that was in a war. Only because he said "Laa ilaaha illa-llaah". He could have said "we were in a war, mistakes happen, so let such a mistake be" (as people now say "in war"). No, the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam gave the family one hundred camels.
And when a woman from Banoe Makhzoem stole, Usaamah ibn Zayd came to the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam and said to him: "O Messenger of Allaah, can you lighten her punishment for her?" And her punishment was the cutting of the hand. So the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam became angry. He said to him: «أتَشفَعُ في حَدٍّ من حُدودِ الله؟» "Do you intercede regarding one of the hudood (prescribed limits/punishments) of Allaah?" Then he stood and said to the people: «يا أيُّها الناس، إنَّما أَهلَكَ الذينَ قبلَكم أنَّهم كانوا إذا سَرَقَ فيهم الشريفُ تَرَكوه، وإذا سَرَقَ فيهم الضعيفُ أقاموا عليه الحَدّ. وايمُ الله، لو أنَّ فاطمةَ بنتَ محمَّدٍ سَرَقَت لقَطَعتُ يَدَها». "O people, indeed what destroyed those before you is that when the noble one among them stole, they left him, and when the weak one among them stole, they established the hadd upon him. And by Allaah, if Faatimah the daughter of Muhammad were to steal, I would cut off her hand." Faatimah was the daughter of Muhammad sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam, and she was, as the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam described her, the best of the women of Paradise except Maryam the daughter of 3imraan, for she is above her.
The Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam became angry here for two matters:
The first matter is that the woman stole, from Banoe Makhzoem. And Banoe Makhzoem were a distinguished family in Quraysh, having a high standing.
That Usaamah ibn Zayd came interceding for her because she was of high standing.
This is a problem that we should also take into account as male teachers and female teachers and educators, that we not leave a distinguished person as he is because we say "his father pays us a lot, his mother/his father does a lot for us in the mosque". No, that [person] you should treat completely like any other person. This is among the matters that destroyed many mosques and destroyed many lessons in the mosques. The teacher does not punish a person because his father spends on the mosque. This is what destroys people. Why have all those mosques never produced good, or a righteous person [who grows up to be] a person of knowledge? Many mosques have graduated people who are huffaadh (those who memorised the Qur'aan). Many of those who memorised the Qur'aan may be in prison or in the criminal milieu because no tarbiyah took place. What comes from the fathers was taken into account more, instead of occupying oneself with the tarbiyah. We now have the responsibility; such a consideration we are not permitted to adopt. And this applies also between you and your partner. If you are occupied with the partner, then do not go considering "if I advise him he will not give me what I want. Then he will not buy me a beautiful dress or a niqaab." Or that the man says to himself "I will not become angry at her, I leave her alone, so if she gives me what I want, then only will we talk." This is not for the sake of Allaah. This must not be present in the family, because this will harm the family too and harm the children too.
And among the ways in which this is practised is that the mother says "if I go now and address him, I get a lot of headache, I will not address him." By this you destroy yourself and your children.
The following definition (the second definition) concerns the long-term solutions and the short-term solutions that the educator should adopt as measures when improving the mistakes and also so that the mistakes are not repeated.
Question: If you sneeze during the prayer, is it permissible that we say "al-hamdu li-llaah"?
The answer: You say to yourself "al-hamdu li-llaah", that is narrated, but it is not permissible for anyone to answer you [to say tashmiet to you]. And you should also not say it in a raised voice.
Imaam at-Tirmidhie narrated that Rifaa3ah said: I prayed behind the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam and I sneezed, then I said: "al-hamdu li-llaah hamdan kathieran [tayyiban] mubaarakan fiehi..." So when the Messenger of Allaah sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam completed his prayer he said: «من المُتَكَلِّمُ في الصلاة؟» "Who is the one who spoke in the prayer?" He heard him. So no one said anything. Then he said: "Who is the one who spoke in the prayer?" So no one said anything. He said: "Who is the one who spoke in the prayer?" So Rifaa3ah said: "I, O Messenger of Allaah." He said: "How did you say it?" He said: "al-hamdu li-llaah hamdan kathieran tayyiban mubaarakan fiehi mubaarakan 3alayhi..." (much good praise, blessed in it and blessed upon it, as our Lord loves and is pleased with). That is a hamdalah at the peak.
Then the Messenger of Allaah sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam said: «والذي نفسي بيده، لقد ابتَدَرَها بِضعةٌ وثلاثونَ مَلَكًا أيُّهم يَصعَدُ بها». "By the One in whose hand is my soul, some thirty-odd angels hastened to it, [competing] which of them would ascend with it." That is, more than thirty angels raced over who would take it from them and ascend with it. This hadieth was graded hasan (good).
The Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam says: «إذا عَطَسَ أحدُكم فلْيَحمَدِ الله». "If one of you sneezes, let him praise Allaah."
Question: You mentioned a universal way [of Allaah] that as long as the people command one another with good, Allaah does not destroy the people. Where do we find the evidence?
The answer: Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa says: «وما كان ربُّك ليُهلِكَ القُرى بظُلمٍ وأهلُها مُصلِحون». Interpretation of the meaning: «And your Lord would not destroy the towns unjustly while their people were reformers.» And the meaning of that then is that when their people are not reformers, all are destroyed. That is [in] Soerat Hoed (117). And this applies also to the family and the household. When the family reforms one another, then Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa will never destroy such a family.
Question (outside the subject matter of the lesson): Can you explain what a woman should do if (it is deemed likely that) she cannot make up the fasting days of last Ramadaan before the coming Ramadaan because of pregnancy?
The teacher: The question: what is the reason that she could not fast?
The sister: Pregnancy.
The teacher: The whole of Ramadaan?
The sister: Yes.
The teacher: Then it is not required of her to make up. She should pay a fidyah (ransom/expiation) for every day. The fidyah is feeding a needy person food that is sufficient for him for one day. That is, food. This can also be given to an institution: for example the SOS institution. But you should explain that it is a fidyah for Ramadaan and that it should be paid out before the coming Ramadaan. They then determine how much money you should pay out for every day, because the amount depends on the country in which they pay it out. It is best that you yourself search for poor people around you.
The sister: When is a person poor?
The teacher: When it is difficult for him to obtain his food. For example the people who come to the food bank. And they should be Muslims.
Question: Can just anyone take on the role of the murabbi? For instance, towards someone else's children?
Answer: It depends on your bond with those children. If there is [between you and them] an educational bond, then you can certainly do so.
The second definition [is] the definition that complements the first. The complementary aspect for correcting [mistakes]. It consists of the direct steps and actions that the murabbi ought to carry out so that he does not repeat the mistake, or so that the mistake does not begin in the first place. As we just said, [there is] a long-term solution and a short-term solution.
What is the link between the long-term solution and the short-term solution?
The long-term solution is the foundation, the base [the groundwork]. If it is not present, then the short-term solution is not possible, because the short-term solution will then have no effect.
The long-term solution is the base, and the short-term is what you build upon that base.
What is the long-term solution?
The thing that every Muslim ought to carry out to keep his life stable. And the long-term solution here [is] to work on every possibility that improves the mind, the heart and the limbs, and to keep it going as much as one can.
Among that is performing the salaah in its time, and the adhkaar in the morning and in the evening and before sleep and after the salaah and in every situation when one leaves the house and enters it, and enters the bathroom and leaves it, and when one puts on his clothes and takes them off. Those are the adhkaar in general. And the most important of the adhkaar are the adhkaar of the morning and the adhkaar of the evening and those after the salaah, because Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa emphasized them in the Qur'aan.
Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa says in Soerat Qaf (39): «فاصبِر على ما يَقولون، وسَبِّح بحمدِ ربِّك قبلَ طُلوعِ الشمسِ وقبلَ الغُروب، ومن الليلِ فسَبِّحه وأَدبارَ السُّجود [بعدَ الصلاة]». Interpretation of the meaning: «So be patient over what they say, and glorify [Allaah] with the praise of your Lord before the rising of the sun and before the setting, and during the night glorify Him, and after prostration [after the salaah].»
Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa emphasized these times even more thereafter.
Other long-term solutions:
The adhkaar, the salaah, the (recommended) siyaam, the zakaah, gathering knowledge (the seerah, the ahaadieth), sadaqah, reciting/memorizing the Qur'aan, holding oneself to account, seclusion with oneself and reflecting on the blessings that Allaah has given you, and reflecting on the creation of Allaah. Whenever a "universal sign [sunnah kawniyyah]" is mentioned, you should place them under one another.
And what do you think about reflecting on death? The Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam says: «أَكثِروا ذِكرَ هاذِمِ اللذَّاتِ ومُفَرِّقِ الجماعات». "Frequently remember the destroyer of pleasures and the separator of gatherings." Reflecting on the Day of the Hereafter (what happens; how we are gathered, how we are treated when we are gathered, what our state is, how the crossing over the Siraat will be, how Paradise will be, how the Fire will be?). Reflecting on the consequences of sins turns you away from carrying out sins or committing them. Reflecting on attachment to the worldly life. Reordering your priorities for the sake of Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa and being patient in that. Being keen on khushoo3 (that you exert everything in your capacity to improve your khushoo3), doing much istighfaar, filtering your environment (friends, female friends), stopping a close bond with people who do not remember Allaah (even if you have known them since childhood, do not go and be led astray), strengthening your contact more with righteous people (righteous sisters), drawing closer to the people of knowledge. These are not matters that we merely mention like this, but rather matters that we ought to examine, and what it is that we can do more in our lives, and are we doing this in our lives?
Looking into the biographies of the Companions and the scholars, our heroes who pleased Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa, in the way they led the Muslims, and that you try to emulate these heroes instead of us occupying ourselves with people who are not heroes and making our children occupy themselves with people who are not heroes.
If you look at the comprehensiveness of the long-term solution, it is that you make your mind and your heart and your limbs and your tongue occupied only with what they were created for and with what pleases Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa. And that you make your mind and your heart and your limbs and your tongue stay away from everything with which Allaah is displeased.
That [is] the long-term solution, and upon it we should all work daily.
Then you have the direct improvement, that is, the short-term solution.
The short-term solution is the solution in which one knows the causes of committing a sin and tries to avoid them, and in which one also tries to improve the matter at every step he carries out before it becomes an action. That is, in reality here we are speaking of practising the thinking scheme.
Practising the thinking scheme does not begin at the processing of perception; rather it begins at knowing the person and what his characteristics are, and what tempts him and distracts him, and trying to divert the person concerned away from what could lead him to evil by diverting the evil away from him.
For example: if [the matter is] between the man and the woman, that he examines any sins/mistakes that my wife commits. That he places on a list. Then he arranges this list according to the priorities that he ought to work on. Then he goes and looks at what could tempt my wife into such a sin. Then it is important that he examines what he utters that could lead his wife to that sin, or at least give her a passing thought [suggestion] that leads her to such a sin or makes her think about such a sin. All these existing temptations he ought to stop/confront. And also actions that he carries out that could lead her to that matter, and also places that he could go to that would lead her to that matter. All those matters he ought to pay attention to, so that he does not even make her think about such a sin, or cause her a passing thought that awakens such a sin. That is how the murabbi ought to be.
Then he asks how she feels, why she feels this way, and so on, so that the woman too is diverted from evil, and so that even if [there] is a thought, he is able to remove such a thought in the correct manner as we dealt with in the thinking scheme.
And if such a thought is also present, then the man cannot merely try to remove such a thought, but must also try to treat it and look again, because a new source of temptation towards such a sin has arisen. That he practises the thinking scheme completely.
When the man does not begin the improvement except at the action, or even at the habit, then the man at that moment ought to correct himself as well, and it means that he has not fulfilled his responsibility completely. His responsibility begins at what his wife sees, and how she feels, and what she thinks about. That is the man's responsibility. If that is not taken seriously, then the man will have a big problem. Many of the brothers do not know this responsibility, and if they know it they do not know how to implement it, and if they know that, they are too lazy to implement it.
It is also important that these steps be taken, and known, and taken seriously, and realized, and implemented, and that there be patience in them, but also that he communicate with his wife about the way he is following, so that his wife too proceeds in the same direction.
And among the matters that belong to the short-term solution is tawbah.
It is important that you do tawbah more, even for the disliked matters, or for the fact that you did not carry out a recommended matter. Or that you will carry out the minimum of a recommended matter. If you feel that you are very tired for the adhkaar of the evening, then if you carry out one dhikr from the adhkaar of the evening, that too is good. Do not go and deceive yourself by saying "either I do it well or I do not do it at all." That is an old trap of the shaytaan.
It is important that the woman submit herself to this manner of tarbiyah. She ought to thank Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa if she has obtained a husband who raises her in such a manner.
And in what remains, it is important that the problems be solved for the sake of Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa and that the improvement be achieved for the sake of Allaah. Therefore I emphasize once again ikhlaas (sincerity). Ikhlaas is an essential act of the heart, of the utmost importance, which you ought also to carry out with your tongue so that Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa blesses the entire process.
You may need a year for this, and some of them years and some of them months to achieve this. According to the speed with which Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa guides you to it. And that is according to the heart and the skills and the effort you exert in it.
The thinking scheme is originally the short-term solution.
Questions
Question: Why is it called a solution?
Answer: The improvement of the woman, and in the end of the man as well, is what the solution ultimately relates to. Solving a problem. The problem in marriage always has a connection to Islam: either it is against one of the three pillars, or it contradicts all three of these pillars, that is, several pillars of the pillars of marriage, so you ought to work on these pillars in this manner.
The pillars [are] more of a [guiding] indication, and this manner is a detailed manner.
Question: You said that there is no problem in there being [any] differences of opinion between the two partners as long as they are within the sharie3ah (a sister raised this).
The sister means that the eighth key for the mind still needs refinement. The woman ought to enter into her husband's world, she ought to be part of her husband's world, and not place herself outside her husband, and not form a separate front nor a separate world. And that then means that her having a different opinion about something is no problem, in the sense that it does not take her outside her husband's world. The opinion can take her outside her husband's world when the shaytaan exploits that by saying to her "you have an opinion, but your opinion does not count," and it can come from both sides.
It may be that he does not implement her opinion, but her opinion gave him a correct passing thought [suggestion]. Every opinion that opens a door for her to set up a separate front is a bad opinion, even if there is nothing [wrong] in the content of the opinion.
Example: the man does not like garlic, and the woman likes garlic a lot. They may have that opinion. The man can never force the woman "you should not like garlic." That is not valid. And that then means that the woman may keep her opinion, and no one will reproach her for that, but she ought to consider the man. That she does not use garlic in the food or in another way, but when her husband is — for example — away for four or five days, that she asks him "can I now eat garlic" or that she takes permission. There is not a person on earth who always has the same opinion as his partner; those people do not exist. So this is how she places her benefit above her opinion, but she may have a different opinion regarding permissible matters, yet she may not make the opinion a door for the shaytaan. They ought to treat [the matter] in the correct manner, and she ought not to see nobility in removing her opinion or in being content that her opinion is not followed, otherwise she will notice that in her heart.
She ought to say to herself: "I have an opinion, I will explain it to my husband when the opportunity arises, but my benefit and the worship of Allaah are higher than my opinion."
Question: Within Moroccan culture [there] are certain healing rituals. One of those rituals is that you touch that ear with that knife without saying anything.
Answer: In general, [the matter is] that these ways of healing can be divided into three categories:
[That it] has a connection to sihr (magic) (its ruling is major kufr).
[That it not] have a connection to sihr, nor [has it] been established that it benefits. They are superstitions, sorcery, and it is not permissible for you to do it, because at that moment you are attaching yourself to something that is not correct, to something that does not benefit, so you attach yourself to something that belongs to the knowledge of the unseen. You let your heart become attached to such a thing while it is not correct.
Matters that have actually been carried out and have proven that they truly benefit, such as some massage [massage], and some Chinese medical ways, and some very ancient Egyptian medical ways that have proven their result. If they are not connected to sihr and the person does not attach his heart directly to them, then it is permissible to carry out these matters.
Question: Images are being circulated about the incident that happened in New Zealand. Is it permissible to view those images? What is the ruling on that?
Answer: It is not forbidden that such matters be shared, except with people who might cause reckless behaviour, that is, youths who do not know how to deal with this; with them it is not permissible for it to be shared, because by that you inflame their ignorance so that they take revenge because of it, and that is not correct. In that case you would be inflaming other people towards violence, and that is not correct. It is permissible for you to send it to righteous people who fear Allaah and whom you know to be sensible and whom you know supplicate against the one who did that and supplicate for our brothers and sisters who were killed there.
Follow-up question:
A sister asked whether it is permissible for us to supplicate against the perpetrator and against the people who wrong the Muslims.
It is from the Sunnah that you supplicate against these people. The Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam also supplicated against Quraysh, that Allaah would seize them with a severe seizing and kill them. There is no problem with the du3aa-e [against them]. It is not correct that you supplicate for their guidance.
We are not Christians who claim that they show nothing but love while they have no love. We are Muslims who ought to be just and to act with this justice. This justice means that we ought to act according to the Sunnah. Whoever harms the Muslims and mutilates them in this hideous manner and kills them, such a person ought to be supplicated against. If the Islamic states truly possessed strength, they would have to do far more. We are now in Holland, and we now at this moment have a connection to Islamic states that are not strong, so it is important [to supplicate].
The Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam supplicated against Aboe Lahab, and against people who wronged him and killed him as well. That is different from the Companions who fought the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam in war and then later embraced Islam. That is very different.
Follow-up question: How, then, is the case with 3umar ibn al-Khattaab? He too was an enemy, and was supplicated for? The Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam did not supplicate for him [specifically]. 3umar was not a wrongdoer like the one against whom the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam supplicated. 3umar in his times of ignorance was against the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam, but the Prophet did not supplicate for him specifically. The Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam supplicated: «اللهمَّ أَعِزَّ الإسلامَ بأَحَبِّ هذين العُمَرَين إليك». "O Allaah, honour Islam with the more beloved of these two 3umars to You." As for Aboe Djahl, when he wronged, he supplicated against him.
Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa is the One who judges between people, so that [they may know] — the people in this world too — that Allaah is the One who is able to remove such wrongdoing or protect from wrongdoing. It is not correct that you supplicate only for him [for guidance].
The Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam made a supplication: «اللهمَّ أَحصِهم عَدَدًا، واقتُلهم بَدَدًا، ولا تُغادِر منهم أَحَدًا» "O Allaah, count them in number, and kill them one and all, and do not leave any of them" (that is: O Allaah, count them in number, and kill them all, and do not leave any of them remaining); this is a supplication that the Prophet taught us.
Indeed, the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam even supplicated against those who did not ask before issuing a ruling, where the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam said: «قَتَلوه، قَتَلَهم الله». "They killed him, may Allaah kill them." If the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam does this with Muslims, then how about a disbeliever who deliberately wars against Islam.
The homework
Organizing your notes and studying them for at least two hours.
We just dealt with a number of steps for the woman to attain a correct perception. These steps begin with "1) Examining any sin that the woman commits and arranging this sin according to the priority of removing it."
2.1 The married sisters
These steps: the married women [must] have these steps clarified to the partners, the husbands; the married women [are] to explain these steps to the husbands and to help their husbands implement these steps with them as well. Next week the intention is that they inform us that they implemented them; we may not know the details, but we also want to know whether their implementation succeeded. And also regarding removing the bad passing thoughts. That is, in reality we will practise step zero, and step 1, and step 2 of the thinking scheme.
2.2 The unmarried sisters will practise this matter with people whom they are able to raise.
2.3 A third type of sisters, the unmarried sisters who do not have [between them and anyone] a relative to whom they have an educational bond, so it is important that they do that with themselves, such that they practise these steps with themselves. Looking into the sins, arranging them according to priorities, then looking at what led to these sins.
The steps are:
Examining any sins/mistakes that my wife commits.
That he places that on a list.
Then he arranges this list according to the priorities that he ought to work on.
Then he goes and looks at what could tempt my wife into such a sin.
Then it is important that he examines what he utters that could lead his wife to that sin, or at least give her a passing thought that leads her to such a sin or makes her think about such a sin. All these existing temptations he ought to stop/confront.
And also actions that he carries out that could lead her to that matter, and also places that he could go to that would lead her to that matter.
All those matters he ought to pay attention to, so that he does not even make her think about such a sin, or cause her a passing thought that awakens such a sin. That is how the murabbi ought to be.
The coming lesson — in shaa-e Allaah
Next week we will speak about the steps towards talaaq.
We move on to another topic: the steps towards improvement, and if improvement is not possible, then towards talaaq. And we will also speak about the types of talaaq, and the types of faskh (annulment of the marriage) of the marriage, and what the rights and duties are.
Until we then begin a new third phase, which is the tarbiyah of the children.
Lesson fifty — Sunday, 24 March 2019
The homework
Organizing your notes and studying them for at least two hours.
We just dealt with a number of steps for the woman to attain a correct perception.
The steps are:
Examining any sins/mistakes that my wife commits.
That he places that on a list.
Then he arranges this list according to the priorities that he ought to work on.
Then he goes and looks at what could tempt my wife into such a sin.
Then it is important that he examines what he utters that could lead his wife to that sin, or at least give her a passing thought that leads her to such a sin or makes her think about such a sin. All these existing temptations he ought to stop/confront.
And also actions that he carries out that could lead her to that matter, and also places that he could go to that would lead her to that matter.
All those matters he ought to pay attention to, so that he does not even make her think about such a sin, or cause her a passing thought that awakens such a sin. That is how the murabbi ought to be.

Next week the intention is that they inform us that they implemented them; we may not know the details, but we also want to know whether their implementation succeeded. And also regarding removing the bad passing thoughts. That is, in reality we will practise step zero, and step 1, and step 2 of the thinking scheme.
2.2 The unmarried sisters will practise this matter with people whom they are able to raise.
2.3 A third type of sisters, the unmarried sisters who do not have [between them and anyone] a relative to whom they have an educational bond, so it is important that they do that with themselves, such that they implement these steps with themselves. Looking into the sins, arranging them according to priorities, then looking at what led to these sins.
Discussion of the homework (24 March 2019)
Discussion of student 1
I asked my brother's daughter [my relative], the seventeen-year-old, what occupies her and from where she draws her inspiration. She said that social media is one of the biggest sources, Islamic and otherwise. She watches lectures via YouTube. And in the Islamic field, what does social media mean to her. She does not follow the lessons via social media, but she indicated that via Instagram and [vlog] clips on YouTube she is also affected by them and that they affect the course of her thinking.
The teacher: In the religious field or another field?
The sister: Sisters who see the hijaab as a piece of fashion. The hijaab is then displayed in a particular way. That affects the course of my relative's thinking, even though she wears the correct hijaab. She develops a weaker faith, and she may also incline towards such a style in dress. She indicated whether she could stop looking at that. She would like to follow the life of these people.
The teacher: It is forbidden for you to look at that. It is forbidden in Islam that you see the sin and be interested in it. Especially when you notice that you are affected by it in your thinking. In that case you are aware of the danger, and it is more strictly forbidden for the one who is aware of it. You are in danger, and Allaah has said: «ولا تَقرَبوا الزِّنا». Interpretation of the meaning: «And do not go near zinaa (fornication/adultery).» This is a definition for every sin. Everything that brings you closer to a particular sin is forbidden, even if in itself it is not a sin. When it is not generally a sin, but you know that it will affect you towards a sin, then it is forbidden for you.
A person came to Imaam Ahmad and said: Is it permissible for me to carry a knife? He saw that he was angry and his face was red. He said: No, it is not permissible. And another person came and posed the same question, and that person appeared calm, so he said: It is permissible. When you carry a knife, there is no problem in using it for cooking, whereas the knife could lead you to a sin, so in carrying the knife there is something not correct.
Most people are not broad-chested [open] when [the matter] is within the family circle, so they are a little shy. You truly have [between you and her] an educational bond.
The sister: I have that with several female relatives.
Then I asked her; she has just begun in units of lessons in the local mosque (As-Salaam mosque in Gouda [Gouda]). The first unit is about the fundamentals of knowing Islam. It is taught by [so-and-so] from [the Al-Yaqeen foundation]. Through these lessons she came to see that Islam consists of many matters that were on her mind. And her female friends too she gathered [invited] to what she learned that Friday, and she also makes them enthusiastic about registering for the coming lessons.
At the second step the sister indicated to her — at the part where she is affected by YouTube — that she ought to do the isti3aadhah (seeking refuge in Allaah) when she is inclined to follow them. And she had said that she must stay away from that website.
The teacher: That belongs beforehand to step zero (at the perception). That she ought not to have such perceptions anymore, and that she stops Instagram except for admonitions or the sites through which admonitions are given. Social media remains a severe fitnah. In it is literally every kind of filth. Originally such media ought not to be used at all. Among the matters that the teacher recommended to the brothers and sisters in the [lesson of] family affairs on Wednesday: Stop social media, for it is nothing but enticing to temptations, sexual temptations, false news, and backbiting. It fills your life with evil and corruption, and by that it fills your heart and your head with it as well.
The teacher no longer enters Facebook except if he wants to publish a post [an advertisement]; he publishes and leaves.
It is important to delete Facebook and YouTube completely. With YouTube you also have another possibility, which is a paid application called "youtuzz" [youtuzz]. This application you fill with your playlists, and your channels that you want, then you can select from them. You can import a file, a program, and according to what you have placed in that file you can watch that video without advertisements and without referrals. This the teacher uses at home for the children.
YouTube itself has a new version, but you have to be very technical to set it up.
You also have other programs. If you can set it up, then set it up; otherwise use social media as little as possible, or do not [use it] at all except — for example — WhatsApp or a chat program with which you can talk to people. And apart from this advice, if she is a subscriber to something, a member of a Facebook [page] that publishes such [content], then she ought to stay away from it. That is an Islamic obligation. The danger of social media extends much further. For every "like" you are held to account before Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa. Because through the like you carried others to that. You carried other people to seeing what you saw, even of evil. So it is very dangerous.
The sister: And finally the sister had discussed with her relative that she finds what is happening in the world terrifying. After those attacks in New Zealand she indicated that she began to dig deeper into the religion and to think about it more. Especially the Day of Resurrection; that increased her faith.
The teacher: Did you also see certain passing thoughts in her speech, and did you indicate that she must beware of them and that this manner of speech arises from what she was affected by? It is important that one examine what he utters and what could lead the woman to sin.
The sister: She indicated that she noticed — when she sees certain clips on YouTube — that she is afraid of being affected by them. In that case she caught the passing thought to ignore it and to stay away from the website/YouTube.
The teacher: It would be good for you to give her the rest of the advice.
Discussion of student 2
The sister carried out the homework task with herself, because she did not have anyone [between her and whom] there was an educational bond. She looked at herself and carried out the homework with herself. She examined for herself any sin she commits, and made a list, and what the priority in it is and what she ought to treat first. One thing came out as the foremost, which is that in certain situations negative thoughts occur to her. They are not negative thoughts about others, but relate to herself. She thought about where they come from, but she does not know, except that she is very aware of them. For a while now, and that she catches herself that it is a negative thought and why [do] you have that. And also that it is an incorrect thought; in that case she does tawbah as well and supplicates to remove those feelings from her heart. [There] are certain situations in which they occur and she notices them, and they are not situations that she can avoid, because they are ordinary daily situations. Avoiding those places she found difficult.
The teacher: Did you not think about the origin of these thoughts?
The sister: Yes, but she was unable to arrive at anything in that. She stopped at where they come from, but she has no idea where they come from. That she found difficult. She examined whether certain sayings are said that lead to that, and [the matter] was so. Those sayings are said by others, not by her, so she was unable to avoid them from that side. They are negative thoughts about herself.
The teacher: It would be good for you to examine this with one who has knowledge who answers you on this.
The sister: She thought about how she can solve this. She remained aware to watch herself and to keep the steps in her mind.
The sister examined with herself how she can solve this, and that she did by means of the thinking scheme, by staying aware and watching herself.
[There] is a certain perception that comes from her environment; the passing thought brings it to her, and it is the negative thought that persists, and that thought is not correct.
The teacher: Did you not think about the perception that you have at that moment?
The sister: Yes, but they are often certain situations that arise and she notices them. Perceptions of daily situations. Not at something specific. She did much tawbah and keeps making that supplication in the prostration and at other moments. The thought depends on faith. She ought to work on her faith more so that that negative thought does not occur. That she did. She thought a lot about the greatness of Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa, and seeing the signs of Allaah, and among what also helped was reading the Qur'aan in the morning after Fadjr. When she would read those verses, [there came over her] an amazement that she felt. It would descend into her heart directly and cause much khushoo3 towards Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa, and that helped against the negativity during the day. She noticed that the more she did that, the better [the matter] was.
And among what she also did was that she took a course in washing the dead. That was a very good reminder, and there was also the possibility that one be wrapped in a shroud and lie down in a coffin that is actually closed. She chose to do that because she wanted to be confronted [with death]. Since she did that, it is truly a vast difference.
The teacher: The Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam does not say in vain: «اذكُروا هاذِمَ اللذَّاتِ ومُفَرِّقَ الجماعات». "Remember the destroyer of pleasures and the separator of gatherings." Remember death frequently so that one knows that he is here only for a moment, not forever, so that he may be diverted on the Day of Resurrection from the Fire. When you remember death you know that you are here only for a moment. You never know when death will strike you. And the other sister said that her relative was affected such that she came to think more about gathering knowledge because of the events/attacks in New Zealand.
The teacher:
From Soerat al-Ahqaaf to Soerat an-Naas is what was first revealed to the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam. These soerahs are for increasing faith as well, where one can explore the greatness of Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa.
Discussion of student 3
The sister discussed the homework with her husband. They thought together about the aim of the homework.
The aim: That she not go and think about the sin, or that he not even cause her a passing thought that awakens such a sin.
Then we determined the priorities according to the weight of the sin/mistake. Naming the temptation and the passing thought and the actions that lead to the sin/mistake was the hardest of it. We made a table with six cells [columns]: the sins/mistakes, the priorities, the temptation, the passing thought, the actions, and the solution.
In the past week we were focused on the sin/mistake that received the first priority. I notice that it improved. The sin occurs less, but it has not yet been removed completely. I think this needs a longer time. We think it is because of little faith.
The teacher: "Little faith" is very general. It could be [the matter] because of different types of temptations mixed with one another, or that at that moment you did not plan something to do, so you were tempted despite that, or that [there] is someone in your environment who leads you to this matter without being aware of it, because he is speaking about a certain topic. It could be various things. You ought to search in a concrete manner for the thing that tempts you, because the shaytaan always uses it to tempt you. It need not be one thing, but rather it could be various things.
You ought to be attentive to these matters that we do in our daily life, because the shaytaan leads to them and our own selves bring us to them. When we are attentive to them we ought not to approach the matters that tempt us, because when we approach them we are drawn inside. The Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam said about the straight path: he drew a straight line, and on the two sides walls, and at every wall doors upon which curtains are hung. And above this path [there] is one who says to the one walking on this path: "Do not deviate, because when you draw aside one of these curtains you are drawn inside." These walls are the limits of Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa — the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam says — and the doors are the doors of the haraam, and the curtains are what tempts a person. They are not closed doors.
Every haraam is a door upon which is a curtain; you are curious what is behind it, so you are drawn inside. You ought not even to think about taking such a turning, but rather walk straight ahead. You ought to look at what tempts you in order to look at that turning. What tempts you to that, you ought to find it and avoid it. If you do this with yourself, it will be easy with your child. And when your husband does this with you, you too know to understand him better. You ought to discuss it with him. "Speaking about a certain topic tempts me to a thought, and that thought carries me to a sin." In that case your husband knows not to [speak] about that topic.
Discussion of student 4
The sister is able to have more patience and to become angry more slowly. And as for the ways to that, she notices that it helps a lot to read the Qur'aan in the morning after Fadjr, especially from Soerat al-Ahqaaf, and to keep performing the adhkaar, and when she has a matter, to present it to the teacher. She indicates that a certain tranquillity comes to her so as to respond to situations with less agitation.
Continuation of the previous lesson
Every righteous deed that strengthens your faith is a matter that belongs to the long-term solution and forms a foundation of the utmost importance for improving mistakes. [There] are two different types of deeds:
Deeds that you can carry out daily.
Deeds connected to time.
Such as going to the mosque, and siyaam, and Hadj, and other deeds connected to time.
The good murabbi uses all the possibilities at that moment regarding the daily deeds. It is important that the murabbi have a form of a table for himself in which he can see what time he is in, which Islamic date, and which acts of worship are connected to it. For example: when one is in [Dhoe] al-Hidjdjah, the first ten [days] are the most important days in which you can carry out righteous deeds and in which you can fast. 3aashoeraa-e, and the Day of 3arafah, and when [the matter] relates to the three white days, and so on.
Originally you ought, as a Muslim, to have an annual schedule in which you can know at which [time] I am (in which time I am) and how I can benefit from the time I am in. That is of the utmost importance.
Task [assignment]
Whoever can make a form of a table in which there are certain deeds dependent on time, that is, dependent on the Islamic date. A kind of calendar (it need not necessarily be a calendar), for example in the month of Safar, in the month of ..., then for each month deeds narrated in the Sunnah that can occur [in it].
<< Saliemah, and Nawaal, and Ming. They will organize it and send it. Do not forget the pure intention in this.
Question about the task
Do you have a trustworthy website in which there are ahaadieth about the months?
Islamway.com, islamweb.net, islaamqa, alaluka (a green website [al-Alukah]).

chapters.title_nl: Vervolg van het oplossen van problemen

chapters.title: ٦) تَوَقَّع الخَطَأ وخُمولَ من تُرَبِّيه

sections.content:
لماذا ينبغي أن تَتوقَّعَ ذلك؟ أوَّلًا لأنَّه أمرٌ بشَريّ. ثانيًا لأنَّ مثلَ هذا الشخصِ على الأرجحِ مُعتادٌ على ذلك ويَلزَمُه أيضًا وقتٌ ليَتَغَيَّر.

حين لا تَتوقَّعُ أنَّه سيُخطِئُ، فستكونُ أحدَ شخصَين: إمَّا أن تذهب في تلك اللحظةِ تَثِقُ ثقةً عَمياءَ بأنَّ [الأمرَ] يَجري جيِّدًا في تلك اللحظة، وذلك يُسَبِّبُ تَراخيًا من المُرَبِّي بحيث لا تَعودُ تُتابِعُ من تُرَبِّيه وتَنظُرُ هل يَفعَلُ جيِّدًا، بحيث يُخطِئُ مرَّةً أخرى كثيرًا ويَبقى باستمرارٍ في عادته السَّيِّئة. ذلك يُسَبِّبُ مرَّةً أخرى تثبيطَ المُرَبِّي، ويمكن أن يُسَبِّبَ في النهايةِ أيضًا تثبيطَ من يُرَبَّى.

تثبيطُ المُرَبِّي لأنَّ ذلك [الشخصَ] يقولُ حينئذٍ «هذا الشخصُ فَشِلَ، أو أنا فَشِلتُ فلن أُحاوِلَ بعد ولن أَتبَعَ الشخص».

وعند من يُرَبَّى: «فَشِلتُ فلا أستطيع، حاوَلتُ فلا أستطيع».

من هو قائدٌ حقيقيٌّ لا يَفعَلُ ذلك. يَبقى يُتابِعُ ذلك [الشخصَ]، لأنَّه حين لا يَفعَلُ جيِّدًا يستطيع أن يُنَبِّهَه مباشرةً نحوَ الإيجابيّ.

وهناك جانبٌ آخرُ يمكن أن يَؤولَ إليه [الأمرُ]، وهو أنَّ المرءَ يَنزَعِجُ من هذا الشخصِ الذي يُرَبَّى فيذهب يَستَجيبُ على وجهٍ خاطئ، على وجهٍ أَقسى، بحيث لا يَعودُ الشخصُ المعنيُّ الذي يُرَبَّى يَرغَبُ في أن يُحَسَّنَ فيُعانِد.

فكِلا الاتجاهَين، كِلا العاقبتَين تَدميرٌ للتربية. يقولُ النبيُّ صلَّى الله عليه وسلَّم في حديثٍ صحيح: «كلُّ بني آدمَ خَطَّاء». خَطَّاء [كثيرو الخطأ]. لم يَقُل صلَّى الله عليه وسلَّم «يُخطِئون»، لا، بل يُخطِئونَ باستمرار، «وخيرُ الخَطَّائينَ التَّوَّابون». احرِص على أن تَسوقَ ذلك الشخصَ كلَّ مرَّةٍ نحوَ إظهارِ التوبة.

يقولُ النبيُّ صلَّى الله عليه وسلَّم: «لكلِّ عملٍ شِرَّةٌ، ولكلِّ شِرَّةٍ فَترة، فمن كانت فَترتُه إلى سُنَّتي فقد اهتَدى، ومن كانت فَترتُه إلى غيرِ ذلك فقد هَلَك». [بمعنى: من وَجَّهَ نشاطَه نحوَ هدفه أو قُربِ هدفه، فذلك من ينبغي أن تَتوقَّعَ منه كثيرًا، ومن أُشيرَ إليه بالأصابع فلا تَتوقَّع من مثله شيئًا.]

أي إنَّ شخصًا يُحاوِلُ أن يَصِلَ نحوَ رضا الله سبحانه وتعالى وحين لا يَنجَحُ يكونُ على الأقلِّ قد حاوَل. ذلك شخصٌ سيَبلُغُ [مُرادَه]، أمَّا شخصٌ يريد دائمًا أن يكون كامِلًا مِثاليًّا فلن يَبلُغ.

كلُّ إنسانٍ عنده أخطاؤُه، ومن يُرَبِّي ينبغي أن يكون صابرًا أيضًا في تحسينِ الأخطاءِ وألَّا يَستَسلِمَ سريعًا أو [يَدَعَ] هذه الأخطاءَ تَستَفِزُّه.

حين تَتوقَّعُ الخَطَأ، فينبغي أيضًا أن تُخَطِّطَ كيف ستُحَسِّنُ ذلك [الشخصَ] إن أَخطَأَ هذا الخَطَأ مرَّةً أخرى. ذلك يَحرِصُ على أنَّ التربيةَ التي تُؤَدِّيها حينئذٍ مُنَظَّمةٌ وتُساقُ في الاتجاهِ الصحيحِ لأنَّك فَكَّرتَ فيها، وحين تذهب تَتصرَّفُ باندفاعٍ ولا تُفَكِّرُ في أنَّ مثلَ هذا الشخصِ سيُخطِئُ الخَطَأَ نفسَه، فإنَّك حَتمًا ستُخطِئُ أنت أيضًا بوصفك مُرَبِّيًا وستكونُ أَكثَرَ انقيادًا للعاطفةِ وتصرُّفًا باندفاعٍ مما لو تَوَقَّعتَ الخَطَأ.
